Emergency coronary angiography with percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) is the definitive therapy
Provide respiratory support: noninvasive positive pressure ventilation or endotracheal intubation
Vasopressors (norepinephrine) to restore mean arterial pressure > 65 mm Hg
Add inotropes (dobutamine or milrinone) to enhance myocardial contractility if perfusion inadequate
**Refractory shock despite medical therapy:** mechanical circulatory support (impella, IABP, or ECMO)

Obtain blood and urine cultures prior to starting antimicrobial therapy
Administer empiric broad-spectrum intravenous antibiotics within one hour of recognition
Administer rapid intravenous fluid resuscitation with isotonic crystalloids
**Hypotension refractory to fluid bolus:** initiate intravenous norepinephrine to maintain MAP >= 65 mm Hg
**Refractory vasopressor dependence:** add vasopressin or low-dose intravenous hydrocortisone
Achieve source control (remove infected catheters, drain obstruction or abscess)

c-im-08-q048.hinge: Point B is closest to the upper-left corner of the ROC curve, maximizing sensitivity and specificity.

B.fit: Here: closest to upper-left corner, optimal sensitivity and specificity

nodes.text: Plot true positive rate (sensitivity) against false positive rate (1 - specificity)
Area under the curve (AUC) quantifies overall test discriminatory accuracy (1.0 = perfect)
Identify the optimal operating cutoff point maximizing the Youden index (sensitivity + specificity - 1)
**Cutoff closest to upper-left corner (Point B):** achieves the best balanced diagnostic accuracy
**Leftward shift along curve (Point A):** increases sensitivity (ideal for screening)
**Rightward shift along curve (Point E):** increases specificity (ideal for confirmation)
Select clinical cutoff based on test purpose: screening vs confirmatory diagnosis

A.tempting: interpreting negative result as excluding malignancy

B.fit: Not here: LR of 1.0 provides no discrimination between presence and absence of cancer
B.tempting: assuming a medical test provides definitive truth

C.fit: Not here: LR of 1.0 does not increase the probability of disease
C.tempting: assuming positive result indicates true disease

E.fit: Here: test research demonstrates likelihood ratio of 1.0

nodes.text: Calculate likelihood ratio (LR+ = sensitivity / [1 - specificity]; LR- = [1 - sensitivity] / specificity)
Post-test odds = pre-test odds * likelihood ratio (Fagan nomogram application)
**Likelihood ratio = 1.0:** post-test probability equals pre-test probability; test provides zero diagnostic utility
**LR > 10 or LR < 0.1:** produces large and conclusive shifts in disease probability
**LR 5-10 or LR 0.1-0.2:** produces moderate shifts in disease probability
Do not order tests with LR = 1.0 because results cannot alter clinical decision-making
Counsel asymptomatic average-risk women that routine ovarian cancer screening is not recommended

algorithm.title: Palliative care and end-of-life symptom management

nodes.text: Terminal cancer patient with refractory disease: clarify goals of care and assess capacity
Respect patient autonomy: competent patients retain full right to refuse disease-directed therapy
Initiate intravenous morphine therapy immediately for severe pain (score 10/10) and dyspnea
**Breakthrough pain occurs:** titrate short-acting parenteral opioid boluses
Provide compassionate communication and family counseling regarding palliative transition
**Family conflict persists despite clarification:** engage hospital palliative care team or ethics
Establish hospice care with advance directives (DNR/DNI) and comfort measures

acute-coronary-syndromes.name: Acute coronary syndromes
acute-coronary-syndromes.scope: Unstable angina, NSTEMI, STEMI, cardiac biomarkers, risk stratification (HEART/TIMI), antiplatelet and anticoagulation, reperfusion
acute-coronary-syndromes.core: Acute myocardial ischemia from coronary plaque disruption: distinguish occlusive infarction needing immediate reperfusion from non-ST-elevation syndromes needing risk-guided invasive management.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Smoking, diabetes, hypertension, dyslipidemia, CKD, age, premature family CAD
Cocaine/stimulants, anemia, tachyarrhythmia may provoke ischemia; distinguish supply-demand injury from plaque rupture

rows.label: Clues
items: Pressure with arm/jaw radiation, diaphoresis, nausea; older adults/diabetes may have dyspnea alone
Inferior MI with hypotension, clear lungs, raised JVP → suspect RV infarction
★ New murmur, pulmonary edema, shock after MI → **mechanical complication**, urgent echo

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Platelet activation and thrombin-mediated clot reduce coronary perfusion; necrosis releases troponin
Type 2 MI: oxygen mismatch without acute atherothrombosis; treat precipitating cause

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **ECG within 10 minutes**, repeat if nondiagnostic; serial high-sensitivity troponin using validated pathway
Posterior suspicion → V7–V9; inferior MI → right-sided leads; new LBBB alone insufficient for STEMI
★ **Do not wait for troponin before STEMI reperfusion**; bedside echo if diagnosis/complications uncertain
HEART ≤3 + negative serial troponins → low risk; TIMI/GRACE stratifies NSTE-ACS

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Chewed aspirin**, P2Y12 inhibitor, anticoagulant such as heparin, high-intensity atorvastatin; oxygen only if hypoxemic
Nitroglycerin for pain unless hypotension, RV infarction, or recent PDE5 inhibitor; avoid NSAIDs
★ STEMI → **primary PCI** within 90 minutes at PCI center, ≤120 minutes including transfer
IF PCI delay >120 minutes, symptoms <12 hours, no contraindication → fibrinolysis promptly, then transfer

rows.label: Complications
items: VT/VF, AV block, HF, cardiogenic shock; papillary rupture, septal rupture, free-wall rupture
Later aneurysm/thrombus, embolism, Dressler syndrome; antithrombotics → bleeding

rows.label: Prevention
items: DAPT usually 12 months after ACS unless bleeding risk changes plan; cardiac rehabilitation, smoking cessation
ACE inhibitor/ARB for LV dysfunction; beta-blocker when stable, avoid in shock or acute decompensation

rows.label: Mimics
items: Aortic dissection: abrupt tearing pain/pulse deficit; anticoagulation or lysis dangerous
Pericarditis: positional pleuritic pain, diffuse changes
PE: hypoxemia, thrombotic risk, RV strain

table.title: Syndrome branches
rows: Urgent catheterization if unstable; otherwise risk-guided angiography
Regional ST elevation or occlusion equivalent
Prior intracranial hemorrhage, active bleeding, suspected dissection

adult-immunizations.name: Adult immunizations
adult-immunizations.scope: Routine adult vaccines, immunocompromised and HIV, pregnancy, live-vaccine contraindications, chronic medical conditions (COPD, diabetes, liver disease), vaccine counseling and addressing hesitancy
adult-immunizations.core: Match vaccination to age, prior doses, pregnancy, immune status, and exposure risk; missed series resume without restarting.

rows.label: Who
items: ★ **HepB**: all adults 19–59; ≥60 with risk or requesting protection
Liver disease → HepA/HepB; COPD, diabetes, smoking → pneumococcal before routine age
Asplenia → pneumococcal, MenACWY, MenB, Hib; HIV → MenACWY

rows.label: Start/stop
items: ★ Pregnancy: **Tdap each pregnancy at 27–36 wk**; inactivated influenza any trimester
Maternal RSV: Abrysvo at 32–36 wk, September–January; previous pregnancy dose → infant antibody instead
RSV once: all ≥75; ages 50–74 with increased severe-disease risk

rows.label: Test
items: Review records, contraindications, immunity; HBV serology useful, but **do not delay vaccination**
★ Immunocompromised ≥19 → recombinant zoster; HIV CD4 ≥200 permits MMR/varicella if nonimmune
HPV started <15 → two doses; ≥15 or immunocompromised → three

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **Avoid live MMR, varicella, intranasal influenza** during pregnancy or severe immunosuppression
PCV15 → PPSV23: minimum 8 weeks if immunocompromised; mild illness/antibiotics need no deferral
Hesitancy → elicit concern, explain benefit, recommend clearly; refusal → document, revisit

table.title: Routine adult schedule
rows: Annual influenza; updated COVID-19 for all adults
Tdap once, then either every 10 years
PCV20/21 alone; PCV15 → PPSV23 after 1 year

anaphylaxis.name: Anaphylaxis
anaphylaxis.scope: Anaphylaxis, angioedema, biphasic reactions, epinephrine autoinjector, emergency airway management
anaphylaxis.core: Rapid multisystem reaction after exposure—or isolated hypotension or airway compromise after a known allergen—requires epinephrine immediately.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Foods, insect venom, antibiotics, latex; exercise can amplify food-triggered reactions
Asthma, prior severe reaction, mast-cell disorders; beta-blockers can complicate treatment

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Urticaria/angioedema + wheeze, stridor, hypotension, or severe GI symptoms**
Skin findings may be absent; hoarseness and tongue swelling predict airway danger
Biphasic recurrence after apparent resolution, especially after severe or undertreated episodes

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Mast-cell/basophil mediators → vasodilation, capillary leak, bronchoconstriction; often IgE-mediated

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Clinical diagnosis**; never wait for tryptase or laboratory confirmation
Acute and baseline serum tryptase can support uncertain cases; normal results do not exclude anaphylaxis

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **IM epinephrine 0.01 mg/kg**, adult 0.3–0.5 mg, lateral thigh; repeat every 5–15 minutes
Supine with legs elevated unless respiratory distress; oxygen, IV saline, early intubation for progressive obstruction
Refractory shock → monitored IV epinephrine infusion; beta-blocker-associated refractory reaction → glucagon
Albuterol for residual bronchospasm; antihistamines relieve itching only; steroids do not reliably prevent biphasic reactions
★ Monitor until resolved; **longer observation/admission** after hypotension, repeated epinephrine, or severe asthma

rows.label: Complications
items: Asphyxia, distributive shock, arrhythmia, hypoxic brain injury
IV epinephrine bolus errors → ischemia and dangerous dysrhythmia

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Prescribe **epinephrine autoinjector**, demonstrate technique, provide written action plan and allergy referral
Extra device for repeat-dose risk; avoidance, medical alert ID; venom immunotherapy after qualifying sting allergy

rows.label: Mimics
items: Vasovagal episode: bradycardia, pallor, rapid improvement supine
Bradykinin angioedema: no itching/hives; ACE inhibitor or hereditary disease → airway, icatibant/C1 inhibitor

asthma.name: Asthma
asthma.scope: Diagnosis, stepwise therapy, acute exacerbation, exercise-induced bronchoconstriction
asthma.core: Variable episodes of wheeze, cough, dyspnea, and chest tightness from reversible expiratory airflow limitation.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Atopy, family history, allergens, viral infections, smoke, occupational sensitizers
Exercise/cold air, aspirin-sensitive disease, nonselective beta-blockers; assess workplace symptom pattern

rows.label: Clues
items: Nocturnal/early-morning symptoms; normal examination between attacks
★ **Silent chest, exhaustion, altered mentation, rising PaCO2** → impending respiratory failure
Acute attack: low peak flow, accessory-muscle use, difficulty speaking

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Airway inflammation, smooth-muscle constriction, mucus → variable obstruction and hyperresponsiveness
Persistent uncontrolled inflammation → remodeling with incompletely reversible airflow limitation

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Spirometry**: obstruction with bronchodilator FEV1 increase >12% and >200 mL in adults
Normal spirometry with suspicion → repeat during symptoms or methacholine challenge
Exercise challenge: postexercise FEV1 fall >10%; assess baseline control before isolated exercise diagnosis

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Exacerbation → **repeated inhaled albuterol + ipratropium**, oxygen, early systemic glucocorticoids
Severe poor response → IV magnesium; deterioration → intubation; avoid sedatives and routine antibiotics
Exercise symptoms → preexercise albuterol or prescribed ICS-formoterol; persistent symptoms → improve controller
Check technique/adherence before stepping up; uncontrolled despite high-dose ICS-LABA → phenotype-directed biologic referral

rows.label: Complications
items: Status asthmaticus, pneumothorax, respiratory arrest
ICS → thrush/dysphonia; systemic steroids → osteoporosis, hyperglycemia, adrenal suppression

rows.label: Prevention
items: Written action plan, trigger reduction, smoking cessation, spacer; rinse mouth after ICS
★ **No SABA-only treatment or LABA monotherapy**; current GINA differs from older intermittent-asthma teaching

rows.label: Mimics
items: Inducible laryngeal obstruction: inspiratory stridor, inspiratory flow-loop flattening
COPD: persistent obstruction, smoking history
HF: edema, elevated JVP, cardiac findings

atrial-fibrillation.name: Atrial fibrillation
atrial-fibrillation.scope: Rate and rhythm control, stroke prevention (CHA2DS2-VASc), unstable AF, embolic complications
atrial-fibrillation.core: Disorganized atrial activation produces an irregularly irregular ventricular rhythm and left atrial appendage thromboembolism risk.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Age, hypertension, heart failure, coronary disease, obesity, sleep apnea
Hyperthyroidism, alcohol binges, infection, postoperative stress, mitral valve disease

rows.label: Clues
items: Palpitations, exercise intolerance, dyspnea; sometimes incidental or first detected after stroke
★ **Hypotension, ischemic chest pain, pulmonary edema, altered mentation** → unstable AF
Very rapid irregular wide-complex rhythm suggests preexcitation; ordinary AV nodal blockers can be dangerous

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Pulmonary-vein ectopic triggers plus atrial remodeling sustain reentry
Loss of atrial contraction reduces filling; persistent tachycardia can impair LV function

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **ECG: absent discrete P waves**, variable RR intervals; document rhythm rather than pulse alone
TSH, electrolytes, renal function; transthoracic echocardiogram for ventricular function and structural disease
Intermittent symptoms → ambulatory rhythm monitoring; assess reversible triggers

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Unstable → **synchronized cardioversion**; do not delay for anticoagulation or TEE
Stable rate control: metoprolol or diltiazem; avoid diltiazem/verapamil with reduced EF
Decompensated HF: digoxin or amiodarone; preexcited AF: procainamide or cardioversion, no AV nodal blockers
Rhythm control for symptoms, early disease, or HF: cardioversion, selected antiarrhythmics, catheter ablation
★ Duration ≥48 hours/unknown: **3 weeks anticoagulation or TEE** before elective cardioversion; ≥4 weeks afterward

rows.label: Complications
items: Systemic emboli to brain, mesentery, limbs; tachycardia-mediated cardiomyopathy
Anticoagulant bleeding; rhythm drugs may cause proarrhythmia

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Long-term anticoagulation: **CHA₂DS₂-VASc ≥2 men/≥3 women**; consider one point lower
Apixaban/other DOAC preferred; mechanical valve or moderate/severe rheumatic mitral stenosis → warfarin
Weight reduction, BP/OSA treatment, limit alcohol; aspirin does not substitute for anticoagulation

rows.label: Mimics
items: Atrial flutter: sawtooth atrial activity, often regular 2:1 conduction
Multifocal atrial tachycardia: ≥3 P-wave morphologies, isoelectric intervals

benign-prostatic-hyperplasia.name: Benign prostatic hyperplasia
benign-prostatic-hyperplasia.scope: Lower urinary tract symptoms, medical therapy, urinary retention and obstructive uropathy
benign-prostatic-hyperplasia.core: Aging man with hesitancy, weak stream, incomplete emptying, and nocturia from benign periurethral prostatic enlargement.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Increasing age, androgen exposure, family history, obesity/metabolic syndrome
Anticholinergics, opioids, and sympathomimetic decongestants can precipitate retention

rows.label: Clues
items: Storage symptoms: urgency, frequency; voiding symptoms: straining, intermittency, terminal dribbling
Smooth, symmetric enlarged prostate; size correlates imperfectly with symptom severity
★ **Painful inability to void** with palpable bladder → acute urinary retention
Renal dysfunction or bilateral hydronephrosis suggests high-pressure obstruction

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Dihydrotestosterone-driven transition-zone hyperplasia + alpha-adrenergic smooth-muscle tone obstruct bladder outlet

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Urinalysis**, symptom score, examination; review medications and neurologic disease
Postvoid residual if incomplete emptying suspected; creatinine/renal ultrasound for obstruction or renal impairment
PSA after shared decision-making if result changes management; elevation not specific for cancer

rows.label: Tx
items: Mild, nonbothersome → observation; reduce evening fluids, caffeine, alcohol; timed voiding
★ Acute retention → **urethral catheter**, then alpha-blocker and voiding trial; suprapubic drainage if catheterization fails
★ Refractory symptoms, retention, recurrent UTIs, stones, renal impairment → **TURP or other outlet procedure**
Monitor urine output/electrolytes after relief of prolonged obstruction

rows.label: Complications
items: Overflow incontinence, recurrent infection, bladder stones, postrenal AKI
Postobstructive diuresis; surgery → bleeding, retrograde ejaculation, urethral stricture

rows.label: Prevention
items: Avoid precipitating drugs; reassess progressive symptoms and residual volume
BPH does not transform into prostate cancer; continue independent cancer-risk discussion

rows.label: Mimics
items: Prostate cancer: hard asymmetric nodule
Prostatitis: tender prostate, fever; neurogenic bladder: neurologic disease, altered bladder sensation

table.title: Medication selection
rows: Large gland; reduce progression over months

bronchiectasis.name: Bronchiectasis
bronchiectasis.scope: Cystic fibrosis, post-infectious, high-resolution CT, airway clearance, pseudomonas colonization, acute exacerbation
bronchiectasis.core: Chronic productive cough with recurrent respiratory infections and permanently dilated bronchi on high-resolution CT.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Cystic fibrosis, prior severe pneumonia/TB, primary ciliary dyskinesia, aspiration, immunodeficiency
ABPA, rheumatoid arthritis, obstructing endobronchial lesion; some cases remain idiopathic

rows.label: Clues
items: Copious purulent sputum, coarse crackles, recurrent focal infections, hemoptysis, sometimes clubbing
Exacerbation: increased sputum volume/purulence, cough, dyspnea, fatigue; hypoxemia or sepsis → severe disease
Early lifelong infections, sinusitis, infertility, or situs inversus suggest impaired ciliary clearance

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Impaired mucus clearance → persistent infection and neutrophilic inflammation → irreversible airway wall destruction

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **High-resolution chest CT**: signet-ring bronchi, absent tapering, airways visible near pleura
Sputum bacterial and mycobacterial cultures; spirometry measures associated airflow limitation
Quantitative immunoglobulins; total IgE/Aspergillus testing for ABPA; sweat chloride if CF suspected
Localized disease → bronchoscopy for tumor/foreign body; diffuse disease → investigate systemic cause

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Daily **airway clearance**, exercise; bronchodilator for obstruction; no routine inhaled steroids or non-CF dornase alfa
★ Exacerbation → sputum culture then antibiotics guided by prior isolates; often **14 days**
Pseudomonas susceptible → ciprofloxacin; severe infection → IV cefepime or piperacillin-tazobactam
★ ≥2 yearly or ≥1 severe exacerbation → azithromycin after NTM exclusion; chronic Pseudomonas → inhaled tobramycin
Massive hemoptysis → airway protection and bronchial artery embolization; focal refractory disease → resection evaluation

rows.label: Complications
items: Chronic Pseudomonas colonization, resistant infection, respiratory failure, pulmonary hypertension
Antibiotic toxicity/resistance; macrolides can cause QT prolongation and hearing impairment

rows.label: Prevention
items: Smoking cessation, influenza/pneumococcal vaccination, aspiration management, treatment of underlying immunodeficiency
New Pseudomonas isolation → specialist eradication regimen, often ciprofloxacin followed by inhaled antibiotic

rows.label: Mimics
items: Chronic bronchitis: smoking-related sputum without characteristic bronchial dilation
Lung abscess: focal cavitary lesion with air-fluid level
Pulmonary TB: constitutional illness and compatible imaging; mycobacterial testing confirms

chronic-kidney-disease.name: Chronic kidney disease and end-stage renal disease
chronic-kidney-disease.scope: CKD progression, anemia of CKD (erythropoietin deficiency), mineral and bone disorder, uremic complications, volume overload, indications for emergent dialysis (AEIOU), vascular access
chronic-kidney-disease.core: Persistent kidney injury or reduced filtration causes progressive cardiovascular, metabolic and uremic complications; dialysis follows clinical indications rather than creatinine alone.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Diabetes, hypertension, glomerular disease, obstruction, recurrent AKI, inherited cystic disease
NSAIDs, smoking and uncontrolled proteinuria accelerate progression

rows.label: Clues
items: Early disease often asymptomatic; advanced disease → fatigue, pruritus, anorexia, edema
Uremia: confusion, pericardial friction rub, nausea or bleeding despite normal platelet count
Labs: normocytic anemia, hyperkalemia, metabolic acidosis, ↑phosphate, low/normal calcium

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Nephron loss → hyperfiltration in remaining nephrons, proteinuria and fibrosis
↓Erythropoietin causes anemia; phosphate retention/↓calcitriol → secondary hyperparathyroidism and renal bone disease

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **eGFR <60** or kidney-damage markers for **≥3 months** establishes CKD
Urine albumin/creatinine ratio, urinalysis, creatinine trend; ultrasound for size/obstruction
Stage by GFR and albuminuria; small echogenic kidneys support chronicity but are not universal
Monitor CBC, ferritin/TSAT, K, bicarbonate, calcium, phosphate and PTH

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Albuminuric CKD → **ACE inhibitor/ARB**; monitor creatinine/K; never combine both
SGLT2 inhibitor for T2DM or qualifying albuminuric CKD/HF, generally starting eGFR ≥20
Overload → salt restriction, furosemide; high phosphate → sevelamer; selected severe hyperparathyroidism → calcitriol
Iron repletion before ESA for selected persistent anemia; correct clinically significant metabolic acidosis
★ **Dialysis (AEIOU)**: refractory acidosis/hyperkalemia/overload, dialyzable toxins, uremic complications

rows.label: Complications
items: Cardiovascular death, fractures, severe hyperkalemic arrhythmia, malnutrition
Dialysis access infection/thrombosis; rapid urea reduction → dialysis disequilibrium

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Preserve arm veins; plan **AV fistula** before hemodialysis; temporary catheter for emergencies; early transplant referral
BP/glycemic control, avoid nephrotoxins, renal drug adjustment; hepatitis B vaccination before dialysis

rows.label: Mimics
items: AKI: acute creatinine change; may complicate established CKD
Prerenal azotemia: reversible perfusion deficit without persistent structural injury

diagnostic-test-accuracy.name: Diagnostic test accuracy
diagnostic-test-accuracy.scope: Sensitivity, specificity, PPV, NPV, likelihood ratios, cut-off changes
diagnostic-test-accuracy.core: Diagnostic accuracy: classification performance against a reference standard; distinguish detection ability from the probability that a result reflects disease.

rows.label: Definition
items: TP/FP: diseased/nondiseased testing positive; FN/TN: diseased/nondiseased testing negative

rows.label: Interpret
items: ★ ↑Prevalence → **↑PPV, ↓NPV**; sensitivity/specificity unchanged if disease spectrum unchanged
★ Positive above threshold: **lower cutoff → ↑sensitivity, ↓specificity**; raising cutoff reverses
LR+ >10 rules in strongly; LR− <0.1 rules out strongly

rows.label: Use when
items: ★ Pretest odds = p/(1−p); **posttest odds = pretest odds × LR**
Posttest probability = odds/(1+odds); pretest 20%, LR+ 4 → odds 1 → 50%
Parallel tests, either positive → ↑sensitivity; serial tests, both positive → ↑specificity

rows.label: Compare
items: ROC: sensitivity versus 1−specificity; AUC 0.5 = chance, 1 = perfect

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **Sensitive negative** helps exclude; specific positive helps confirm; neither absolute
Case-control sampling → PPV/NPV unrepresentative without population prevalence
Verification bias: reference testing only selected results → distorted accuracy

diagnostic-test-accuracy.evidence: Established statistical definitions; no guideline-dependent recommendation.

dyslipidemia.name: Dyslipidemia
dyslipidemia.scope: Lipid screening guidelines, ASCVD risk calculation, statin therapy indications, monitoring response to diet and pharmacotherapy
dyslipidemia.core: Excess atherogenic lipoproteins drive ASCVD; treatment intensity follows established disease, severe LDL elevation, diabetes, and estimated absolute cardiovascular risk.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Familial disorders, saturated-fat intake, obesity, diabetes, hypothyroidism, nephrotic syndrome, cholestasis
Premature ASCVD family history, CKD, smoking, inflammatory disease increase treatment benefit

rows.label: Clues
items: Usually asymptomatic; tendon xanthomas/early corneal arcus suggest familial hypercholesterolemia
Severe triglyceride elevation: eruptive xanthomas, pancreatitis; low HDL alone is not a drug target

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Retained apoB-containing particles → arterial inflammation and plaque formation
Statins inhibit HMG-CoA reductase → hepatic LDL-receptor upregulation

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Lipid panel from age 19, at least every 5 years**; earlier/more often with risk
Nonfasting panel acceptable; markedly high triglycerides → fasting repeat/secondary-cause evaluation; Lp(a) once/lifetime
★ **PREVENT-ASCVD**, ages 30–79, LDL 70–189 without ASCVD: replaces pooled-cohort equations in 2026 guidance
Uncertain statin decision → coronary calcium; zero insufficient for deferral with diabetes, smoking, strong premature history

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Clinical ASCVD or **LDL ≥190 mg/dL → high-intensity statin**, no risk calculation required
★ Diabetes age 40–75 → **at least moderate-intensity statin**; multiple risk factors favor high intensity
Above LDL target despite maximal statin → ezetimibe; consider PCSK9 inhibitor or bempedoic acid
Severe triglycerides ≥500 → address causes, diet, consider fenofibrate/prescription omega-3 to reduce pancreatitis risk

rows.label: Complications
items: MI, stroke, peripheral arterial disease; statins → myalgias, rare rhabdomyolysis, small diabetes-risk increase
Baseline ALT; CK only with symptoms/risk; most lipid-lowering drugs deferred during conception/pregnancy/lactation

rows.label: Prevention
items: Mediterranean-style diet, replace saturated fats, exercise, weight reduction, smoking cessation
★ Recheck lipids **4–12 weeks after starting/changing drugs**, then every 6–12 months; assess adherence
High intensity lowers LDL ≥50%: atorvastatin 40–80 mg or rosuvastatin 20–40 mg

rows.label: Mimics
items: Hypothyroidism: elevated TSH; correct before labeling primary dyslipidemia
Nephrotic syndrome: heavy proteinuria, hypoalbuminemia; treat renal cause

giant-cell-arteritis.name: Giant cell arteritis
giant-cell-arteritis.scope: Giant cell arteritis, polymyalgia rheumatica, vision loss
giant-cell-arteritis.core: New headache with jaw claudication or visual symptoms after age 50 requires immediate glucocorticoids to prevent irreversible blindness.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Older age, female sex, Northern European ancestry; frequently overlaps polymyalgia rheumatica
Age <50 makes this diagnosis very unlikely

rows.label: Clues
items: Scalp tenderness, abnormal temporal artery, fever, weight loss, fatigue
★ **Transient monocular loss, diplopia, or sudden painless visual loss** → ocular ischemia
PMR: bilateral shoulder/hip aching, morning stiffness >45 minutes; true muscle strength preserved

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Granulomatous inflammation of large/medium arteries → intimal proliferation and ischemic narrowing
Posterior ciliary artery involvement causes arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **ESR/CRP and CBC**: inflammation, thrombocytosis, normocytic anemia support; normal markers do not fully exclude
★ **Temporal artery biopsy** confirms; skip lesions can cause false negative, so obtain adequate segment
Ultrasound halo sign useful in experienced centers; arrange testing promptly after treatment begins
Assess pulses, arm pressures, bruits; CTA/MRA for suspected aortic/branch-vessel involvement
PMR: elevated inflammatory markers, normal CK; screen all PMR patients for cranial/visual symptoms

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Suspected cranial GCA → **high-dose oral prednisone now**, before biopsy
★ Threatened or established visual loss → **IV methylprednisolone** urgently; ophthalmology consultation
Taper slowly with symptom/marker monitoring; tocilizumab can reduce steroid exposure in selected patients
Isolated PMR → lower-dose prednisone; failure to improve promptly → reconsider diagnosis

rows.label: Complications
items: Permanent blindness, often sequential fellow-eye involvement; stroke, aortic aneurysm/dissection
Prolonged steroids → infection, diabetes, cataracts, osteoporosis; IL-6 blockade can suppress inflammatory markers

rows.label: Prevention
items: Bone protection and fracture-risk assessment during prolonged steroids; monitor BP/glucose
Educate about recurrent visual symptoms, jaw pain, limb claudication; evaluate aorta over time

rows.label: Mimics
items: Nonarteritic ischemic optic neuropathy: vascular risks, no systemic inflammatory syndrome
Myositis: objective proximal weakness, elevated CK
TMJ disease: local joint pain/clicking rather than chewing-induced ischemic fatigue

giant-cell-arteritis.evidence: Not checked online; established rheumatologic emergency and PMR management.

gonococcal-infection.name: Gonococcal infection
gonococcal-infection.scope: Urethritis/cervicitis, disseminated gonococcal infection, gonococcal arthritis, neonatal conjunctivitis
gonococcal-infection.core: Neisseria gonorrhoeae causes mucosal infection and can disseminate into a dermatitis-tenosynovitis-arthritis syndrome or purulent septic arthritis.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: New/multiple partners, inconsistent barriers, prior STI, younger age
Complement deficiency increases dissemination risk; neonatal exposure during vaginal delivery

rows.label: Clues
items: Dysuria, mucopurulent discharge, friable cervix; rectal/pharyngeal disease often asymptomatic
★ **Migratory arthralgia, tenosynovitis, sparse pustules** → disseminated infection
Neonate: copious purulent conjunctivitis 2–5 days after birth; corneal injury can progress rapidly

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Gram-negative intracellular diplococci adhere to mucosa; antigenic variation permits recurrent infection
Ascending genital spread or bacteremia extends disease beyond initial exposure site

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **NAAT at exposed sites**: urine/vaginal, rectal, pharyngeal; test chlamydia, HIV, syphilis
Symptomatic male urethral Gram stain may show intracellular diplococci; less reliable at other sites
Dissemination: blood/synovial cultures and mucosal NAAT; negative joint culture does not exclude diagnosis
Suspected treatment failure → culture and antimicrobial susceptibility, assess reinfection

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Uncomplicated: **ceftriaxone 500 mg IM once**; ≥150 kg → 1 g once
Chlamydia not excluded → doxycycline for 7 days; pregnancy → azithromycin instead
★ Disseminated disease → **IV/IM ceftriaxone**, hospitalization initially; drain purulent joint
Neonatal infection → systemic ceftriaxone, or cefotaxime if bilirubin/calcium concerns; topical treatment alone insufficient

rows.label: Complications
items: PID, infertility, ectopic pregnancy, epididymitis, corneal perforation
Rare endocarditis/meningitis; untreated septic arthritis damages cartilage

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Treat partners from preceding **60 days**; abstain 7 days after treatment and until partners treated
Retest at 3 months; pharyngeal test-of-cure at 7–14 days; routine urogenital test-of-cure unnecessary
Condoms, risk-based screening; neonatal erythromycin eye ointment prevents gonococcal ophthalmia

rows.label: Mimics
items: Chlamydia: similar urethritis/cervicitis, NAAT distinguishes
Reactive arthritis: sterile arthritis after infection, conjunctivitis/enthesitis
Staphylococcal arthritis: usually isolated hot joint without migratory skin-tendon syndrome

gout.name: Gout and crystal arthropathy
gout.scope: Acute gout, chronic gout and urate lowering, pseudogout (CPPD)
gout.core: Abrupt intensely painful inflammatory arthritis from crystal deposition; gout and CPPD require different long-term prevention despite similar flare management.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Gout: CKD, obesity, alcohol, purines/fructose, thiazide/loop diuretics, low-dose aspirin
CPPD: older age, joint injury, hyperparathyroidism, hemochromatosis, hypomagnesemia
Flares follow surgery, dehydration, illness, or changes in urate concentration

rows.label: Clues
items: Rapid-onset red swollen tender joint, often overnight; fever possible
Chronic gout: tophi on ears/olecranon, erosive arthritis; recurrent flares separated by asymptomatic intervals
CPPD in younger adults → investigate associated metabolic disorders

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Crystal phagocytosis activates inflammasome/IL-1 → neutrophilic synovitis
Most hyperuricemia reflects reduced renal urate excretion rather than excessive production

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ First/atypical acute monoarthritis → **arthrocentesis**, polarized microscopy, Gram stain/culture
★ **Crystals do not exclude septic arthritis**; serum urate may be normal during gout flare
Chronic imaging: punched-out defects with overhanging edges; ultrasound double-contour sign supports urate deposition

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Acute either crystal flare → **NSAID, colchicine, or glucocorticoid**; intraarticular steroid only after infection excluded
CKD/ulcer/anticoagulation → favor steroid; adjust colchicine for renal impairment/interactions; avoid NSAIDs in advanced CKD
★ Urate lowering: **allopurinol first-line**, including CKD; start low, titrate to serum urate <6 mg/dL
Continue urate lowering during flares; may start during treated flare; no routine asymptomatic-hyperuricemia treatment

rows.label: Complications
items: Gout: destructive arthritis, uric-acid stones; CPPD: chronic degenerative/inflammatory arthropathy
Allopurinol hypersensitivity; colchicine → diarrhea/neuromyopathy
Xanthine-oxidase inhibitors + azathioprine/6-MP → severe marrow suppression

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Urate lowering: **tophi, joint damage, ≥2 flares/year**; first flare with CKD ≥3/stones/urate >9 → consider
Starting urate lowering → colchicine/NSAID prophylaxis 3–6 months; serial urate monitoring
Weight reduction, limit alcohol/fructose; replace thiazide with losartan when feasible; retain indicated aspirin
Before allopurinol: HLA-B*58:01 testing with Southeast Asian/African American ancestry; CPPD lacks crystal-depleting drugs

rows.label: Mimics
items: Septic arthritis: positive culture, bacteremia risk; aspiration essential when uncertain
Cellulitis: superficial inflammation, less restriction of passive joint motion
RA: persistent symmetric small-joint synovitis

gout.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [ACR gout guideline 2020](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10563586/), [ACR gout education 2025](https://rheumatology.org/patients/gout); CPPD established teaching.

heart-failure.name: Heart failure
heart-failure.scope: HFrEF, HFpEF, acute decompensated heart failure, cardiogenic flash pulmonary edema, guideline-directed medical therapy, neurohormonal activation (RAAS, ADH-mediated hyponatremia)
heart-failure.core: Inadequate cardiac output or elevated filling pressures → pulmonary or systemic congestion, even with a normal ejection fraction.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: CAD, hypertension, valvular disease, cardiomyopathy, alcohol, cardiotoxic chemotherapy
Decompensation triggers: ischemia, infection, arrhythmia, missed diuretics, NSAIDs

rows.label: Clues
items: Orthopnea, paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea, elevated JVP, crackles, dependent edema
S3 suggests volume overload; S4 suggests stiff ventricle
★ **Flash edema**: abrupt respiratory distress, severe hypertension, pink frothy sputum

rows.label: Pathophys
items: RAAS/sympathetic activation → vasoconstriction, sodium retention, adverse remodeling
Nonosmotic **ADH** release → dilutional hyponatremia; marker of advanced disease

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Echocardiography**: EF, valves, wall motion; ECG, CXR, BNP support diagnosis
Low BNP argues against HF; obesity lowers BNP, renal dysfunction raises it
Identify precipitant: troponin, CBC, electrolytes, creatinine; evaluate ischemic cause

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Acute congestion → **IV furosemide**; hypoxemia → oxygen; respiratory distress → noninvasive ventilation
★ Hypertensive pulmonary edema → **IV nitroglycerin**; shock → norepinephrine ± dobutamine, urgent cause correction
Start beta-blocker only when compensated; ACE inhibitor → ARNI requires 36-hour washout
MRA requires eGFR >30, K <5; persistent EF ≤35% despite GDMT → consider ICD

rows.label: Complications
items: Cardiorenal syndrome, ventricular arrhythmia, sudden death, hepatic congestion
Diuresis → hypokalemia; RAAS blockade → hyperkalemia, renal dysfunction; monitor creatinine/K

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Daily weights, sodium moderation, adherence; **continue GDMT after EF recovery**
Treat hypertension, CAD, AF; smoking cessation, exercise, influenza/pneumococcal vaccination

rows.label: Mimics
items: COPD: obstructive spirometry, hyperinflation
Nephrotic syndrome: heavy proteinuria, hypoalbuminemia
PE: pleuritic pain, thrombotic risk, RV strain

heart-failure.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [ACC HFrEF 2024](https://www.acc.org/Latest-in-Cardiology/ten-points-to-remember/2024/03/06/19/22/2024-acc-expert-consensus-hfref); other points established teaching.

herpes-simplex-virus.name: Herpes simplex virus
herpes-simplex-virus.scope: HSV-1 and HSV-2, genital herpes, neonatal herpes, herpes labialis, eczema herpeticum, acyclovir
herpes-simplex-virus.core: Painful grouped vesicles recurring at mucocutaneous sites reflect latent HSV reactivation; neonatal infection and disseminated disease require urgent systemic treatment.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Skin/mucosal contact, asymptomatic shedding, new sexual partners; either HSV type can cause genital disease
Immunosuppression, atopic dermatitis; neonatal risk highest with newly acquired maternal infection near delivery

rows.label: Clues
items: Primary genital episode: fever, tender nodes, dysuria, multiple painful ulcers; recurrences generally milder
Labialis: tingling prodrome around lip; herpetic whitlow: painful finger vesicles
★ **Monomorphic punched-out erosions in eczema** → eczema herpeticum; ocular symptoms threaten vision
Neonate: sepsislike illness, vesicles sometimes absent; seizures/hepatitis suggest CNS or disseminated disease

rows.label: Pathophys
items: HSV establishes sensory ganglion latency; stress, illness, UV exposure trigger reactivation
Genital HSV-2 recurs and sheds more frequently than genital HSV-1

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Active lesion → **HSV PCR/NAAT with typing**; culture less sensitive as lesions heal
CSF HSV PCR for encephalitis/neonatal CNS concern; early negative may require repeat testing
Neonate → lesion/surface, blood, CSF testing plus liver enzymes; start treatment while testing
Type-specific serology only selected situations; no routine population screening or HSV IgM

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ First genital episode → **oral acyclovir or valacyclovir for 7–10 days**
Recurrence → prompt episodic dosing at prodrome; frequent/distressing episodes → daily suppressive valacyclovir
★ Neonatal, CNS, disseminated disease or severe eczema herpeticum → **IV acyclovir**; neonatal duration below
Genital HSV pregnancy: suppress acyclovir/valacyclovir from 36 weeks; lesions/prodrome at labor → cesarean
Corneal involvement → urgent ophthalmology; avoid unsupervised ocular corticosteroids

rows.label: Complications
items: Encephalitis, aseptic meningitis, urinary retention, keratitis, dissemination; increased HIV acquisition risk
Acyclovir → crystal nephropathy, neurotoxicity with renal impairment; hydration and dose adjustment

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Avoid sex during lesions/prodrome**, condoms, partner disclosure; suppression lowers but never eliminates transmission
Avoid kissing infants with active labialis; cover lesions, hand hygiene

rows.label: Mimics
items: Syphilis: classically painless chancre
Aphthae: mucosal ulcers without preceding grouped vesicles
Zoster: unilateral dermatomal eruption rather than recurrent focal mucocutaneous clusters

herpes-simplex-virus.evidence: Checked genital disease 2026-10-30: [CDC HSV guidance](https://www.cdc.gov/std/treatment-guidelines/herpes.htm); neonatal/eczema management established teaching.

table.title: Neonatal IV acyclovir duration
rows: ≥21 days; CNS: confirm CSF PCR clearance

hiv-infection.name: HIV infection
hiv-infection.scope: Acute HIV, testing, ART start, opportunistic infection prophylaxis, PrEP/PEP, opportunistic infections (CMV retinitis, toxoplasmosis, PJP)
hiv-infection.core: HIV progressively depletes CD4 cells; early diagnosis and suppressive ART prevent immune failure and sexual transmission.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Sexual exposure, shared injection equipment, perinatal transmission; other STIs increase acquisition risk

rows.label: Clues
items: Acute infection: fever, rash, sore throat, generalized lymphadenopathy after recent exposure
Weight loss, oral thrush, recurrent infections suggest advanced immunodeficiency

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Retroviral integration creates lifelong reservoirs; ongoing replication drives immune depletion and inflammation

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Fourth-generation Ag/Ab → HIV-1/2 differentiation assay**; discordance → HIV RNA
★ Recent exposure/acute syndrome despite negative screen → **HIV RNA**, before antibodies appear
Baseline viral load, CD4, resistance genotype, renal/liver function, HBV/HCV/TB testing; pregnancy assessment
AIDS: CD4 <200 or AIDS-defining illness regardless of count

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Start **integrase-based ART promptly**, usually bictegravir/TAF/emtricitabine; assess HBV coinfection and interactions
Do not delay routine ART for genotype; cryptococcal/TB meningitis require disease-specific deferred timing
PJP: TMP-SMX; add glucocorticoid if PaO₂ <70 or A–a gradient ≥35
Toxoplasmosis: pyrimethamine/sulfadiazine/leucovorin or TMP-SMX; CMV retinitis: valganciclovir, urgent ophthalmology

rows.label: Complications
items: Opportunistic infections, malignancies, wasting, neurocognitive disease, kidney disease
Immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome after ART; drug toxicity/interactions

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ PJP prophylaxis: **TMP-SMX** with CD4 <200 before/starting ART; on ART, <100 or 100–200 with viremia
Toxoplasma IgG positive + CD4 <100 → prophylaxis; MAC <50 only without immediate effective ART
★ Exposure ≤72 hours → **28-day PEP: dolutegravir + TDF/emtricitabine**; do not delay for laboratory results
PrEP: TDF/emtricitabine, cabotegravir, or lenacapavir; exclude HIV first, continue serial testing

rows.label: Mimics
items: EBV mononucleosis: atypical lymphocytes, heterophile positivity; acute HIV can be heterophile-negative
Primary CNS lymphoma: often solitary brain lesion, fails empiric anti-Toxoplasma treatment

table.title: Advanced-disease syndromes
rows: Dry cough, hypoxemia, ground-glass; induced sputum/BAL

hyperglycemic-crises.name: Hyperglycemic crises
hyperglycemic-crises.core: Insulin-deficient diabetes with osmotic diuresis: rapid acidotic illness or slowly progressive hyperosmolar encephalopathy.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Infection, missed insulin, pump failure, MI; DKA often type 1, HHS often older type 2
Euglycemic triggers: **SGLT2 inhibitors**, pregnancy, fasting

rows.label: Clues
items: Polyuria, thirst, weight loss, dry mucosa, tachycardia
DKA: abdominal pain, vomiting, **Kussmaul breathing**; HHS: profound dehydration, focal deficits
★ Severe: **hypotension, stupor**, or coma → ICU

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Insulin deficit + counterregulatory hormones → lipolysis, ketogenesis; residual insulin in HHS limits ketosis
Total-body K depleted despite initially normal/high serum K

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Glucose, electrolytes, venous pH, β-hydroxybutyrate**, osmolality; ECG + trigger evaluation
Effective osmolality = 2 × Na + glucose/18; glucose in mg/dL
★ HHS: **effective osmolality >300 OR total >320 mOsm/kg**; substantial ketosis/acidosis → mixed DKA/HHS
DKA resolution: ketones <0.6 mmol/L AND (pH ≥7.3 OR HCO₃ ≥18); urine ketones/anion gap misleading

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **IV isotonic crystalloid → K correction → IV regular insulin**; K <3.5 mmol/L → delay insulin
Replace K when <5 mmol/L; glucose checks every 1–2 h, electrolytes/pH/ketones every 4 h
★ Add **dextrose** below glucose 250; euglycemic presentation → immediately; continue insulin until crisis resolves
SC basal insulin overlaps infusion 1–2 h; bicarbonate only consider pH <7.0; HHS: slower osmolar correction

rows.label: Complications
items: AKI, thrombosis; treatment: hypoglycemia, hypokalemic arrhythmias, cerebral edema, hyperchloremic acidosis

rows.label: Prevention
items: Sick-day fluids/ketone checks; continue basal insulin; ensure supplies and early follow-up
Hold SGLT2 inhibitors during acute illness and before surgery

rows.label: Mimics
items: Alcoholic ketoacidosis: binge then poor intake; usually no diabetes
Starvation ketosis: usually milder acidosis, no marked hyperglycemia
Toxic alcohols: osmolar gap, exposure; absent substantial ketonemia

table.title: Biochemistry; ketones and HCO₃ in mmol/L

hyponatremia.name: Hyponatremia
hyponatremia.scope: Hypovolemic, euvolemic (SIADH, primary polydipsia), hypervolemic, acute vs chronic, hypertonic saline indications
hyponatremia.core: Low serum sodium reflects excess water relative to sodium; symptoms and duration determine urgency before the cause determines maintenance treatment.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Thiazides, SSRIs, carbamazepine; postoperative pain, nausea, endurance exercise
Pulmonary/CNS disease, malignancy; heart failure, cirrhosis, renal failure

rows.label: Clues
items: Nausea, headache, gait instability; seizures, coma or marked confusion indicate severe cerebral edema
Orthostasis/dry mucosa suggest depletion; edema/ascites suggest excess extracellular fluid
SIADH: clinically euvolemic with inappropriately concentrated urine despite hypo-osmolality

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Hypotonic extracellular fluid drives water into brain; chronic adaptation makes rapid correction dangerous
ADH-mediated water retention or intake exceeding renal dilution capacity lowers sodium concentration

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Serum osmolality first: **<275 mOsm/kg** confirms hypotonicity; assess glucose and volume status
Hyperglycemia → translocational hyponatremia; severe hyperlipidemia/proteinemia → pseudohyponatremia
★ Urine osmolality **<100** → polydipsia/low solute; ≥100 → persistent ADH activity
Urine Na <20–30 suggests low effective arterial volume; >30 suggests renal loss or SIADH
Exclude adrenal insufficiency, hypothyroidism and renal failure before diagnosing SIADH; diuretics confound urine Na

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Severe neurologic symptoms → **3% saline bolus**, repeated for initial Na rise 4–6 mEq/L
Hypovolemia → isotonic saline; SIADH → fluid restriction, increased solute, remove trigger
Edematous states → fluid/sodium restriction and loop diuretic; treat heart/liver/kidney disorder
★ Chronic/unknown duration: generally limit rise to **≤8 mEq/L per 24 h**; monitor frequently
Overcorrection → desmopressin plus D5W; avoid routine vaptans in acute symptomatic cases

rows.label: Complications
items: Acute severe hyponatremia → herniation, respiratory arrest
Osmotic demyelination after rapid correction; greatest risk with alcoholism, malnutrition, hypokalemia

rows.label: Prevention
items: Avoid hypotonic maintenance fluids during high ADH states; review causative drugs
Monitor for brisk aquaresis after restoring volume or stopping thiazides

rows.label: Mimics
items: Hyperosmolar hyperglycemia: measured osmolality elevated
Primary psychiatric disease: neurologic change without sodium abnormality

hyponatremia.evidence: Not checked online; established hyponatremia consensus principles.

infective-endocarditis.name: Infective endocarditis
infective-endocarditis.scope: Native and prosthetic valve endocarditis, Duke criteria, prophylaxis, IV drug use endocarditis, blood culture diagnostic criteria
infective-endocarditis.core: Persistent bacteremia with valve infection causes systemic emboli, valve destruction, and immune-complex injury.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Prosthetic valve, prior endocarditis, congenital valve abnormality, intracardiac device
Injection drug use → tricuspid involvement; healthcare exposure, indwelling vascular access

rows.label: Clues
items: Fever, new regurgitant murmur, embolic stroke, splenic infarct, hematuria
Janeway lesions painless; Osler nodes painful; splinter hemorrhages nonspecific
★ **New conduction block** → periannular abscess; right-sided disease → septic pulmonary emboli

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Endothelial injury → platelet-fibrin nidus → microbial adherence and vegetation
Immune complexes → glomerulonephritis; infected fragments disseminate through downstream circulation

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Three blood-culture sets before antibiotics**; separate peripheral draws unless resuscitation would be delayed
Major microbiology: **typical organism in ≥2 culture sets**, nontypical in ≥3; specialized serology/PCR also qualifies
★ **TTE → TEE** if prosthesis/high suspicion; major imaging: vegetation, abscess, perforation, new significant regurgitation
Definite clinical Duke: 2 major, 1 major + 3 minor, or 5 minor criteria
Minor: predisposition, fever, vascular phenomena, immunologic phenomena, nondiagnostic microbiology

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Empiric **IV vancomycin + cefepime** for acutely ill/healthcare-associated cases; tailor to cultures and setting
MSSA → nafcillin/oxacillin or cefazolin; susceptible viridans streptococci → ceftriaxone
Prolonged pathogen-directed IV antibiotics; prosthetic infections need specialist regimen and early surgical evaluation
Surgery: heart failure, abscess, persistent bacteremia, fungal infection, or selected recurrent/large embolizing vegetations

rows.label: Complications
items: Acute regurgitation, heart failure, mycotic aneurysm, metastatic infection
Antibiotic nephrotoxicity, line infection; hemorrhage into embolic cerebral lesions

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Dental **amoxicillin** for prosthetic valve/material, previous IE, selected cyanotic/residual CHD, transplant valvulopathy
Good oral hygiene, sterile access; no routine prophylaxis for GI/GU procedures or isolated MVP

rows.label: Mimics
items: Nonbacterial thrombotic endocarditis: cancer/autoimmune disease, sterile cultures
Atrial myxoma: positional obstruction, intracavitary mass; vasculitis: no infected vegetation

inflammatory-bowel-disease.name: Inflammatory bowel disease
inflammatory-bowel-disease.scope: Crohn disease, ulcerative colitis, extraintestinal manifestations (erythema nodosum, pyoderma gangrenosum, uveitis), toxic megacolon, colorectal cancer risk, biologic therapy
inflammatory-bowel-disease.core: Chronic relapsing intestinal inflammation: Crohn disease affects any gastrointestinal segment; ulcerative colitis begins in the rectum.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Family history, young adulthood; smoking worsens Crohn disease
NSAIDs and enteric infections can precipitate flares

rows.label: Clues
items: Chronic diarrhea, abdominal pain, weight loss, anemia; children may have growth failure
Arthritis, uveitis, erythema nodosum, pyoderma gangrenosum; PSC particularly associated with UC
★ Severe colitis: fever, tachycardia, frequent bloody stools; distention suggests **toxic megacolon**

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Dysregulated mucosal immune response to intestinal microbiota in genetically susceptible hosts

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Stool **C. difficile** testing and cultures before attributing worsening diarrhea to inflammation
Fecal calprotectin supports intestinal inflammation; **ileocolonoscopy with biopsies** confirms
Suspected small-bowel disease or abscess → MR enterography; avoid capsule with suspected stricture
Fulminant colitis → abdominal radiograph and limited sigmoidoscopy; avoid full colonoscopy

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Acute severe UC → hospitalization, **IV methylprednisolone**, fluids, VTE prophylaxis
Steroid-refractory severe UC → infliximab or cyclosporine; perforation or megacolon → urgent colectomy
★ Steroids induce remission only; **never maintenance**
Crohn abscess → antibiotics and drainage before immunosuppression

rows.label: Complications
items: Fistulas, strictures, obstruction and B12 deficiency in Crohn; colectomy does not cure Crohn
Colonic disease → colorectal cancer; active inflammation → venous thromboembolism

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Colonic disease → surveillance colonoscopy beginning about **8 years** after onset; PSC → immediately
Vaccinate and screen TB/HBV before biologics; smoking cessation for Crohn

rows.label: Mimics
items: IBS: no bleeding, weight loss or inflammatory markers
Ischemic colitis: abrupt pain followed by hematochezia, vascular risk

interstitial-lung-disease.name: Interstitial lung disease
interstitial-lung-disease.scope: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, hypersensitivity pneumonitis, sarcoidosis, pneumoconioses, restrictive PFTs (reduced DLCO, normal/high FEV1/FVC), high-resolution CT
interstitial-lung-disease.core: Progressive exertional dyspnea, dry cough, and inspiratory crackles suggest diffuse parenchymal lung disease; HRCT patterns and exposure history identify the cause.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Age >60 and smoking: IPF; autoimmune disease; familial fibrosis
Amiodarone, bleomycin, nitrofurantoin; occupational silica/coal/asbestos, organic antigens; prior thoracic radiation

rows.label: Clues
items: Fine basal Velcro crackles, exertional desaturation, later clubbing; systemic rheumatic features can reveal cause
Sarcoidosis: bilateral hilar adenopathy, uveitis, erythema nodosum, sometimes hypercalcemia
Rapidly worsening oxygenation → infection, embolism, edema, or acute exacerbation evaluation

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Alveolar/interstitial injury and aberrant repair reduce lung compliance and gas-transfer capacity
Granulomatous inflammation or fibrogenic dust responses produce distinct imaging distributions

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **HRCT + full PFTs** after chest radiograph; obtain detailed drug, occupation, hobby, autoimmune history
★ **↓TLC, ↓DLCO, normal/↑FEV1/FVC** support restriction; low FVC alone is insufficient
UIP: basal subpleural reticulation, traction bronchiectasis, honeycombing; exclude known causes before labeling IPF
Autoantibodies when connective-tissue disease suspected; BAL/biopsy selected through multidisciplinary review
Typical UIP without secondary cause may avoid surgical biopsy; assess exertional oxygen needs

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Remove offending exposure/drug**, pulmonary rehabilitation, oxygen for hypoxemia; treat identified cause
★ IPF: **nintedanib or pirfenidone** slows decline; no routine chronic prednisone-based immunosuppression
Inflammatory sarcoid/autoimmune disease: selected steroids or steroid-sparing agents; mild sarcoid may need observation
Progressive fibrotic non-IPF disease → nintedanib consideration; advanced disease → early transplant evaluation

rows.label: Complications
items: Pulmonary hypertension, cor pulmonale, respiratory failure, exacerbations; asbestos raises lung cancer/mesothelioma risk
Silicosis increases TB susceptibility; antifibrotics can cause GI adverse effects and liver injury

rows.label: Prevention
items: Smoking cessation, respiratory immunizations, occupational dust controls, medication monitoring; follow FVC/DLCO trends

rows.label: Mimics
items: Heart failure: congestion/cardiomegaly, volume response; emphysema: obstruction with hyperinflation
Neuromuscular restriction: low volumes with relatively preserved diffusion capacity

table.title: Imaging clues to etiology
rows: Centrilobular nodules, mosaic attenuation, air trapping

irritable-bowel-syndrome.name: Irritable bowel syndrome
irritable-bowel-syndrome.scope: Rome IV criteria, IBS subtypes (IBS-C, IBS-D, IBS-M), alarm features, low FODMAP diet, antispasmodics, fiber supplementation
irritable-bowel-syndrome.core: Recurrent abdominal pain linked to defecation and altered stool frequency/form, without alarm findings, supports a positive diagnosis of IBS.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Younger age, female sex, anxiety/depression, adverse life stress, previous enteric infection
Food-related symptom flares common; psychosocial associations do not make symptoms imaginary

rows.label: Clues
items: Bloating, urgency, mucus, incomplete evacuation; stool passage can worsen rather than relieve pain
★ **Bleeding, anemia, weight loss, fever, nocturnal diarrhea**, family cancer/IBD history → evaluate organic disease
New onset in older adults warrants careful assessment and age-based colorectal cancer screening

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Disordered gut–brain signaling, visceral hypersensitivity, altered motility and microbiome contribute
No destructive mucosal inflammation; subtype follows predominant abnormal stool consistency

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Rome IV**: pain ≥1 day/week over prior 3 months, symptom onset ≥6 months earlier
At least two: related to defecation, change in stool frequency, change in stool form
CBC; diarrhea phenotype → celiac serology and fecal calprotectin/lactoferrin ± CRP when no alarms
★ **No routine colonoscopy** in younger patients meeting criteria without warning signs or screening indication
Review medications, lactose intolerance, infectious exposures; stool pathogen tests only when suggested by history

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Soluble fiber/psyllium**, regular meals, exercise; limited low-FODMAP trial with structured reintroduction
Gut-directed CBT/hypnotherapy; peppermint oil may help pain; TCA useful for persistent pain, especially diarrhea
Dicyclomine: selected episodic cramping; anticholinergic harms, weak global-symptom evidence; avoid routine use

rows.label: Complications
items: Quality-of-life impairment, restrictive diets, anxiety; no increased colorectal cancer risk from IBS itself
Eluxadoline: pancreatitis risk, contraindicated without gallbladder; avoid escalating opioids

rows.label: Prevention
items: Identify dietary/stress triggers, maintain activity; avoid prolonged unnecessary elimination diets
Reassess new alarm findings rather than attributing every symptom to established IBS

rows.label: Mimics
items: IBD: objective inflammation/bleeding; celiac: positive serology, malabsorption
Microscopic colitis: watery nocturnal diarrhea, normal-looking colon, diagnostic biopsies

table.title: Stool subtype and targeted treatment
rows: PEG for constipation; linaclotide/lubiprostone for global symptoms
Loperamide for diarrhea; rifaximin for global symptoms

ischemic-stroke-and-tia.name: Ischemic stroke and TIA
ischemic-stroke-and-tia.scope: TIA (including amaurosis fugax), ischemic stroke, acute management (tPA, thrombectomy), secondary prevention, risk factors
ischemic-stroke-and-tia.core: Abrupt focal neurologic loss from cerebral ischemia; transient monocular blindness localizes to the ipsilateral carotid circulation.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Hypertension, smoking, diabetes, dyslipidemia, carotid atherosclerosis
Atrial fibrillation, recent MI, endocarditis, arterial dissection

rows.label: Clues
items: Aphasia or neglect suggests cortical involvement; crossed cranial-nerve/limb findings suggest brainstem disease
★ **Last known well** establishes treatment timing; symptom discovery time may differ
TIA: resolved deficit without acute infarction; urgent evaluation despite normal examination

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Thromboembolism or small-vessel occlusion → infarct core surrounded by salvageable penumbra
Reperfusion preserves threatened tissue but increases hemorrhagic transformation risk

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Fingerstick glucose + **noncontrast head CT** first; normal early CT does not exclude ischemia
CTA head/neck for large-vessel occlusion; MRI diffusion for small infarcts or diagnostic uncertainty
ECG, telemetry, carotid imaging; echocardiography for suspected cardiac emboli

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Disabling deficit, eligible ≤4.5 hours → **alteplase or tenecteplase**; imaging-selected extended windows possible
Thrombolysis: BP <185/110 before, <180/105 after; exclude bleeding and significant anticoagulant effect
★ Large-vessel occlusion → **mechanical thrombectomy**, selected cases through 24 hours; do not delay thrombolysis
No reperfusion: generally allow BP ≤220/120; oxygen for hypoxemia; swallow assessment before oral intake
Aspirin after hemorrhage excluded; after thrombolysis, wait 24 hours and repeat imaging

rows.label: Complications
items: Cerebral edema, aspiration, venous thrombosis, seizures, disability

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Minor noncardioembolic stroke/high-risk TIA → short **aspirin + clopidogrel**, then single antiplatelet
AF → oral anticoagulation with timing based on infarct/bleeding risk; high-intensity statin, BP control
Symptomatic carotid stenosis 70–99% → endarterectomy when eligible; selected 50–69% also benefit

rows.label: Mimics
items: Hypoglycemia: deficit reverses with glucose
Migraine aura: spreading positive symptoms; seizure: witnessed convulsion followed by Todd paralysis

lung-cancer.name: Lung cancer
lung-cancer.scope: Non-small cell, small cell, paraneoplastic syndromes, Pancoast, screening
lung-cancer.core: Persistent cough, hemoptysis, weight loss, or a suspicious lung lesion requires tissue diagnosis and staging before treatment selection.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Smoking, radon, asbestos, occupational carcinogens, prior thoracic radiation; adenocarcinoma also occurs in never-smokers

rows.label: Clues
items: Recurrent focal pneumonia, hoarseness, clubbing, unexplained pleural effusion
★ **Pancoast tumor**: shoulder/ulnar-arm pain + ipsilateral Horner syndrome
SVC obstruction: facial swelling, neck-vein distention; cord compression or airway compromise requires urgent action

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Bronchogenic malignant transformation → local invasion, lymphatic spread, hematogenous metastasis
Ectopic hormone production and immune cross-reactivity cause paraneoplastic syndromes

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Suspicious finding → **contrast chest CT**; biopsy easiest site that establishes highest stage
Central lesion/nodes → bronchoscopy/EBUS; peripheral lesion → CT-guided biopsy; effusion → cytology
PET/CT for extracranial staging, brain MRI for selected stages/small-cell disease; pulmonary function before resection
Molecular profiling and PD-L1 guide advanced NSCLC treatment; suspicious nodes often require pathologic staging

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Early operable NSCLC → **surgical resection + nodal evaluation**; inoperable localized → stereotactic radiation
Locally advanced NSCLC → combined systemic treatment/radiation ± surgery in selected patients
Metastatic NSCLC → biomarker-directed agents or immunotherapy/chemotherapy
★ Small-cell → **platinum + etoposide**, stage-dependent radiation/immunotherapy; surgery rarely used

rows.label: Complications
items: Brain/bone/adrenal/liver metastases, malignant effusion, thrombosis, respiratory failure
Radiation pneumonitis; checkpoint inhibitors → immune pneumonitis/endocrinopathies

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ USPSTF: **annual low-dose CT**, age 50–80, ≥20 pack-years, current smoking or quit <15 years
Stop after 15 quit-years or limited curative candidacy; **ACS omits quit-time restriction**
Smoking cessation and radon mitigation; chest radiographs do not substitute for screening CT

rows.label: Mimics
items: TB/fungal granuloma: microbiologic evidence; PET uptake not specific for cancer
Hamartoma: fat/popcorn calcification; pneumonia: clinical/radiographic response to antibiotics

lung-cancer.evidence: Screening checked 2026-10-30: [USPSTF 2021](https://www.uspreventiveservicestaskforce.org/uspstf/recommendation/lung-cancer-screening), [ACS 2023 guideline](https://acsjournals.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.3322/caac.21811); treatment: established stage-based framework.

microcytic-anemia.name: Microcytic anemia
microcytic-anemia.scope: Iron deficiency, anemia of chronic disease, thalassemia, sideroblastic anemia
microcytic-anemia.core: Low hemoglobin with MCV <80 fL: distinguish depleted iron, inflammatory iron sequestration, globin underproduction, and defective heme synthesis.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Menstrual/GI blood loss, pregnancy, low intake, malabsorption → iron depletion
Chronic infection, autoimmune disease, malignancy → inflammatory anemia
Inherited hemoglobin disorders; alcohol, lead, isoniazid, myelodysplasia → disordered heme production

rows.label: Clues
items: Fatigue, pallor, exertional dyspnea; severe anemia → tachycardia, angina, syncope
Pica, koilonychia, restless legs suggest iron deficiency
Markedly low MCV with relatively preserved hemoglobin and high RBC count suggests thalassemia trait

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Inflammation → ↑hepcidin → ferroportin suppression, impaired absorption and iron release
Sideroblasts: mitochondrial iron accumulation in erythroblasts from impaired protoporphyrin synthesis

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **CBC/smear → ferritin**, iron, TIBC, transferrin saturation; ferritin rises with inflammation
★ Ferritin **<45 ng/mL in anemia** supports iron deficiency; normal result cannot exclude during inflammation
★ Adult men/postmenopausal women with iron deficiency → **EGD + colonoscopy**; consider celiac testing
Hemoglobin electrophoresis for suspected beta-thalassemia; alpha trait may require genetic testing; exposure → blood lead

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Iron deficiency → **oral ferrous sulfate**; intolerance/malabsorption or rapid replacement need → IV iron
Treat bleeding source; continue iron about 3 months beyond hemoglobin normalization; reassess nonresponse
Inflammatory anemia → treat underlying disease; selected CKD → iron ± erythropoietin
Sideroblastic: remove trigger, pyridoxine if isoniazid-related; severe thalassemia → transfusion/chelation

rows.label: Complications
items: Iron deficiency: developmental effects in children, adverse pregnancy outcomes
Repeated transfusion → iron overload, cardiac/hepatic injury; oral iron → constipation, dark stool

rows.label: Prevention
items: Adequate dietary iron, pregnancy supplementation, lead-exposure reduction
★ **No empiric long-term iron for thalassemia trait** without documented deficiency

rows.label: Mimics
items: Acute blood loss: initially normocytic; hemoglobin may lag volume loss
Hemolysis: reticulocytosis, ↑LDH/indirect bilirubin, ↓haptoglobin

microcytic-anemia.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [AGA iron deficiency evaluation 2020](https://gastro.org/clinical-guidance/gastrointestinal-evaluation-of-iron-deficiency-anemia/); remaining hematology established teaching.

multiple-myeloma.name: Multiple myeloma
multiple-myeloma.scope: CRAB features (hypercalcemia, renal insufficiency, anemia, bone lytic lesions), SPEP/UPEP M-spike, serum free light chains, bone marrow biopsy (>10% plasma cells), MGUS, smoldering myeloma
multiple-myeloma.core: A clonal plasma-cell malignancy causes monoclonal protein production and organ damage; modern biomarkers can establish treatment-requiring disease before symptoms.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Older age, Black ancestry, male sex, preexisting MGUS; usually no identifiable preventable exposure

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **CRAB**: hypercalcemia, renal impairment, anemia, lytic bone lesions
Back/rib pain, pathologic fracture, recurrent bacterial infection, high total protein, rouleaux
Acute weakness/back pain → cord compression; proteinuria or restrictive cardiomyopathy → consider AL amyloid

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Marrow expansion suppresses blood formation; osteoclast activation without osteoblast response causes bone destruction
Monoclonal light chains injure renal tubules; reduced normal immunoglobulins impair defense

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **SPEP/immunofixation + free light chains**, urine studies; light-chain disease may lack serum spike
★ **Bone marrow biopsy** quantifies clonal plasma cells; whole-body low-dose CT/MRI assesses bone disease
Active disease: ≥10% clonal marrow cells/plasmacytoma plus attributable CRAB or myeloma-defining biomarker
SLiM: marrow ≥60%; involved/uninvolved FLC ratio ≥100 with involved FLC ≥100 mg/L
MRI >1 focal lesion ≥5 mm defines active disease; bone scan may miss lytic lesions

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Bortezomib-based combination** ± daratumumab/lenalidomide/dexamethasone; selected patients → autologous transplant
Hypercalcemia → saline plus antiresorptive; AKI → hydration, avoid NSAIDs/contrast and rapidly reduce light chains
Cord compression → dexamethasone and urgent MRI/radiation or surgery; treat infections promptly
MGUS/smoldering disease generally monitored; high-risk smoldering disease merits specialist assessment

rows.label: Complications
items: Cast nephropathy, vertebral collapse, hyperviscosity, AL amyloidosis; treatment-related neuropathy, infections and thrombosis

rows.label: Prevention
items: Vaccines, bisphosphonates; proteasome inhibitors → antiviral prophylaxis; immunomodulators → thromboprophylaxis by risk

rows.label: Mimics
items: Metastatic carcinoma: destructive lesions without clonal plasma-cell findings
Waldenström macroglobulinemia: IgM, hyperviscosity/lymphadenopathy, usually no lytic lesions

multiple-myeloma.evidence: Criteria checked 2026-10-30: [IMWG diagnostic criteria](https://www.myeloma.org/newly-diagnosed/multiple-myeloma-diagnostic-criteria); treatment: established generalist teaching.

myeloproliferative-neoplasms.name: Myeloproliferative neoplasms
myeloproliferative-neoplasms.scope: CML, polycythemia vera, essential thrombocythemia, primary myelofibrosis
myeloproliferative-neoplasms.core: Clonal marrow proliferation elevates mature blood-cell counts or causes progressive fibrosis; thrombosis and transformation drive management.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Usually acquired stem-cell mutations in adults; age and prior thrombosis predict vascular risk
Prior radiation exposure associated with CML; no common lifestyle trigger explains most cases

rows.label: Clues
items: Splenomegaly, fatigue, early satiety, constitutional symptoms; markedly abnormal CBC may be incidental
★ **Aquagenic pruritus**, erythromelalgia or unexplained splanchnic thrombosis → evaluate clonal disease
Very high platelets may paradoxically cause mucosal bleeding through acquired von Willebrand dysfunction

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Constitutive tyrosine-kinase signaling produces growth independent of normal feedback
Myelofibrosis → cytokine-driven fibrosis and extramedullary hematopoiesis; not simply excess fibroblast clonality

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **CBC/smear**, erythropoietin with erythrocytosis; marrow biopsy and mutation testing classify disease
PV thresholds: hemoglobin >16.5 g/dL men/>16 women or hematocrit >49%/>48%, with diagnostic context
ET requires persistent platelets ≥450,000/µL plus marrow/molecular findings and exclusion of reactive causes
Teardrops and leukoerythroblastosis support fibrosis; marrow aspiration may yield dry tap

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ PV → **phlebotomy to hematocrit <45%** plus low-dose aspirin if safe
PV/ET high thrombotic risk → hydroxyurea; interferon favored for selected younger/pregnant patients
★ CML → **BCR-ABL tyrosine kinase inhibitor**, e.g., imatinib; monitor molecular response
Symptomatic myelofibrosis → JAK inhibitor such as ruxolitinib; allogeneic transplant potentially curative
Extreme thrombocytosis with bleeding → assess von Willebrand function before aspirin; urgent cytoreduction if critical

rows.label: Complications
items: Arterial/venous thrombosis, hemorrhage, hyperuricemia; secondary myelofibrosis or AML
CML blast phase: ≥20% blasts; advanced disease needs acute-leukemia-directed specialist treatment

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Cardiovascular risk control; disease-specific count control, pregnancy planning, monitor progression

rows.label: Mimics
items: Reactive thrombocytosis: iron deficiency/inflammation; secondary erythrocytosis: hypoxia or ↑EPO
Leukemoid reaction: toxic granulation, infection trigger, absent BCR-ABL

myeloproliferative-neoplasms.evidence: Not checked online; established clinical teaching.

nephrotic-syndrome.name: Nephrotic syndrome
nephrotic-syndrome.scope: Minimal change, FSGS, membranous, diabetic nephropathy; thrombosis and hyperlipidemia
nephrotic-syndrome.core: Heavy proteinuria with hypoalbuminemia and edema indicates nephrotic syndrome; assess the cause and complications before choosing immunosuppression.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Diabetes, obesity, HIV, hepatitis B/C, autoimmune disease, malignancy and selected medications
Children favor minimal change; obesity, HIV or reduced nephron mass can cause secondary FSGS

rows.label: Clues
items: Periorbital/dependent edema, foamy urine, weight gain; severe cases → anasarca or effusions
Hyperlipidemia, lipiduria, oval fat bodies/fatty casts; urine sediment often otherwise bland
★ Sudden flank pain, hematuria or falling filtration → **renal vein thrombosis**
Low effective volume may coexist with generalized fluid overload

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Podocyte barrier damage leaks albumin; sodium retention and low oncotic pressure promote edema
Urinary loss of anticoagulants and immunoglobulins increases thrombosis and infection risk

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Adult protein **>3.5 g/day** or equivalent spot protein/creatinine ratio; serum albumin and lipid profile
Urinalysis/microscopy, renal function, HbA1c; targeted HIV, HBV/HCV, ANA/complement and monoclonal-protein studies
★ Most unexplained adult cases → **kidney biopsy**; classic childhood minimal change often treated empirically
Anti-PLA2R supports primary membranous disease; assess secondary causes and age-based cancer screening
Diabetes with retinopathy, gradually rising albuminuria → likely diabetic nephropathy; atypical features → consider biopsy

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Salt restriction, **loop diuretic**, ACE inhibitor/ARB for proteinuria; monitor perfusion and K
Eligible CKD → SGLT2 inhibitor; treat diabetes/infection or remove causative drug
Minimal change/primary FSGS → glucocorticoids; secondary FSGS → cause-directed/supportive treatment, not routine steroids
Membranous disease → risk-stratified observation versus rituximab or other immunosuppression
★ Confirmed thrombosis → anticoagulate; preventive anticoagulation individualized by albumin, pathology and bleeding risk

rows.label: Complications
items: DVT/PE, renal vein thrombosis, cellulitis/peritonitis, AKI, accelerated atherosclerosis
Progressive glomerular scarring can lead to kidney failure

rows.label: Prevention
items: Vaccinate, control BP/glycemia, avoid NSAIDs; monitor treatment toxicity and recurrent proteinuria

rows.label: Mimics
items: Nephritic syndrome: dysmorphic RBCs/casts, hypertension, inflammatory sediment
Cirrhosis: low albumin without nephrotic protein loss

table.title: Classic pathology
rows: Diffuse foot-process effacement; normal light microscopy

nephrotic-syndrome.evidence: Not checked online; established nephrology teaching and risk-based treatment principles.

obesity-hypoventilation-syndrome.name: Obesity hypoventilation syndrome
obesity-hypoventilation-syndrome.scope: Alveolar hypoventilation, daytime hypercapnia, normal A-a gradient hypoxemia, cor pulmonale, positive airway pressure
obesity-hypoventilation-syndrome.core: Obesity with awake hypercapnia after exclusion of alternative causes defines obesity hypoventilation syndrome, usually accompanied by obstructive sleep apnea.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Severe obesity, coexistent sleep-disordered breathing; sedatives/opioids may precipitate decompensation
Reduced mobility, cardiopulmonary comorbidity and weight gain increase ventilatory load

rows.label: Clues
items: Daytime somnolence, morning headache, snoring; dyspnea and awake hypoxemia suggest more than isolated OSA
Elevated bicarbonate reflects renal compensation for chronic respiratory acidosis
Peripheral edema, JVD and loud P2 suggest pulmonary hypertension/cor pulmonale
★ Acute lethargy, worsening acidosis or respiratory distress → **acute-on-chronic hypercapnic failure**

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Chest-wall load, reduced compliance and blunted ventilatory drive cause inadequate alveolar ventilation
Pure hypoventilation produces hypoxemia with normal A–a gradient; atelectasis/comorbidity may increase the gradient

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **BMI ≥30 + awake PaCO2 ≥45 mm Hg**, excluding other hypoventilation causes
★ Low/moderate suspicion and **bicarbonate <27 mmol/L** → OHS unlikely; ≥27 → ABG
Strong suspicion → ABG directly; pulse oximetry alone cannot diagnose ventilatory failure
Polysomnography defines OSA severity and guides PAP settings; assess spirometry, thyroid and drug causes
Exclude COPD, neuromuscular weakness, chest-wall disorders and central hypoventilation before assigning diagnosis

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Stable with severe OSA → **CPAP first-line**; persistent hypercapnia or nonobstructive hypoventilation → bilevel PAP
Acute hypercapnic decompensation → **bilevel noninvasive ventilation** if protecting airway; intubate if failing
Hospitalized suspected OHS with respiratory failure → discharge NIV pending prompt sleep assessment/titration
★ Sustained **weight loss**, often bariatric treatment, provides definitive disease modification
Avoid oxygen alone: can worsen CO2 retention; add oxygen only for residual hypoxemia despite adequate ventilation

rows.label: Complications
items: Pulmonary hypertension, right-heart failure, recurrent respiratory admissions and increased mortality
Anesthesia/opioids increase perioperative hypoventilation risk; monitor ventilation after procedures

rows.label: Prevention
items: PAP adherence, weight management and avoidance of respiratory depressants
Coordinate sleep follow-up and cardiometabolic treatment; counsel against drowsy driving

rows.label: Mimics
items: Isolated OSA: daytime PaCO2 generally normal
COPD: obstructive spirometry and smoking history
Neuromuscular weakness: reduced respiratory strength without obesity requirement

palliative-and-hospice-care.name: Palliative and hospice care
palliative-and-hospice-care.scope: Hospice eligibility, pain control, goals of care, surrogate requests
