palliative-and-hospice-care.core: Palliative care relieves suffering at any illness stage; hospice centers care on comfort when prognosis and patient goals support a terminal-care benefit.

rows.label: Principle
items: ★ **Patient goals and informed consent** guide intervention burdens; symptom relief remains an obligation
Proportionate opioids for pain/dyspnea ethically permissible despite foreseeable unintended risks

rows.label: Do
items: ★ Ask understanding/values → discuss prognosis → recommend a goal-concordant plan
Assess capacity; use advance directive, then authorized surrogate: substituted judgment/best interests
★ Titrate **opioids** to symptoms; add stimulant laxative for constipation, reassess sedation/respiration

rows.label: Don't
items: DNR ≠ no antibiotics, fluids, nutrition or other desired treatment
Capable patient’s informed wishes override surrogate requests
No nonbeneficial interventions; explain reasoning, offer alternatives, seek ethics review for conflict

rows.label: Exceptions
items: Refractory terminal suffering → proportional palliative sedation, specialist review and consent
Emergency, unknown preferences → stabilize while clarifying wishes; honor documented refusals

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ Hospice: **≤6-month prognosis** if usual course; longer survival permits recertification
Medicare hospice election concerns terminal-illness treatment; unrelated conditions remain treatable
No DNR requirement for hospice; enrollment can be revoked if goals change

palliative-and-hospice-care.evidence: Eligibility checked 2026-10-30: [CMS hospice benefit](https://www.cms.gov/medicare/payment/fee-for-service-providers/hospice); clinical ethics: established teaching.

pancreatic-cancer.name: Pancreatic cancer
pancreatic-cancer.scope: Pancreatic adenocarcinoma, painless jaundice, Courvoisier sign, CA 19-9, neuroendocrine tumors (gastrinoma, insulinoma)
pancreatic-cancer.core: Older adult with weight loss and painless obstructive jaundice, or persistent epigastric pain radiating to the back.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Smoking, chronic pancreatitis, obesity, increasing age; strong family history, hereditary cancer syndromes
New diabetes with unexplained weight loss can signal occult malignancy

rows.label: Clues
items: Head lesions: dark urine, pale stools, pruritus, nontender palpable gallbladder (**Courvoisier sign**)
Body/tail lesions: late presentation with pain and cachexia; migratory thrombophlebitis may occur

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Ductal adenocarcinoma causes biliary obstruction, perineural invasion, and early metastatic spread
Pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors arise from endocrine cells; may be functional or incidental

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Pancreatic-protocol CT** for mass, vessels, metastases; ultrasound may initially show biliary dilation
EUS biopsy before systemic treatment/uncertain diagnosis; not mandatory before straightforward resection
★ **CA 19-9** monitors disease; neither screening nor definitive diagnosis; obstruction can falsely elevate
Resectability depends on metastases and major vascular involvement; MRI clarifies indeterminate liver lesions

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Resectable head tumor → **Whipple**; body/tail tumor → distal pancreatectomy; add systemic chemotherapy
Borderline resectable → neoadjuvant treatment; metastatic → systemic treatment and palliation
★ Cholangitis → **urgent ERCP**; unresectable symptomatic jaundice → biliary stent
Analgesia, pancreatic enzymes for malabsorption, nutritional support

rows.label: Complications
items: VTE, biliary infection, gastric outlet obstruction, exocrine insufficiency, diabetes
Resection → pancreatic fistula, delayed gastric emptying, malabsorption

rows.label: Prevention
items: Smoking cessation; no average-risk population screening; selected hereditary high-risk patients → MRI/EUS surveillance

rows.label: Mimics
items: Choledocholithiasis: colicky pain, ductal stone
Autoimmune pancreatitis: IgG4 elevation, diffuse pancreatic enlargement
Chronic pancreatitis: calcification, recurrent pain, prior inflammation

table.title: Functional neuroendocrine tumors
rows: ↑Insulin/C-peptide during supervised fast; negative sulfonylurea screen

pancreatic-cancer.evidence: Not checked online; established pancreatic oncology teaching.

pancreatitis.name: Pancreatitis
pancreatitis.scope: Acute pancreatitis, chronic pancreatitis, exocrine and endocrine insufficiency
pancreatitis.core: Epigastric pain radiating to the back with pancreatic inflammation may be acute; repeated injury produces irreversible chronic insufficiency.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Gallstones, alcohol, triglycerides >1,000 mg/dL, ERCP, hypercalcemia, medications
Chronic: prolonged alcohol/tobacco exposure, genetic disease, duct obstruction, autoimmune disease

rows.label: Clues
items: Severe constant pain, vomiting, tenderness, ileus; chronic disease adds steatorrhea and weight loss
★ **Hypoxemia, hypotension, oliguria, persistent SIRS** → early monitored/ICU assessment

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Premature intrapancreatic enzyme activation → autodigestion and systemic inflammation
Chronic fibrosis destroys acinar/islet tissue; lipase may normalize despite advanced disease

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Acute diagnosis: **2 of 3**—typical pain, lipase ≥3× ULN, characteristic imaging
RUQ ultrasound evaluates gallstones; triglycerides, calcium, liver tests identify cause
Contrast CT for uncertain diagnosis, deterioration, or failure to improve after 48–72 hours; not routine immediately
Chronic: CT/MRCP shows calcification/duct changes; fecal elastase <200 supports exocrine insufficiency

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Acute: **moderate lactated Ringer resuscitation**, frequent reassessment, analgesia, electrolyte correction; avoid overload
★ **Early oral low-fat feeding** within 24–48 hours if tolerated; enteral tube feeding if unable
Biliary with cholangitis → urgent ERCP; mild gallstone disease → cholecystectomy before discharge
Sterile necrosis: no antibiotics; infected: penetrating antibiotics, delayed step-up drainage/debridement
Chronic: stop alcohol/tobacco; pancreatic enzymes, nutrition/fat-soluble vitamins, pain and diabetes management

rows.label: Complications
items: ARDS, AKI, shock, hypocalcemia; local necrosis, vascular thrombosis, hemorrhage
Pseudocyst after >4 weeks; infected collection, obstruction; chronic disease → pancreatic cancer and brittle diabetes

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Treat cause**: gallbladder removal, triglyceride control, avoid culprit drug and alcohol
Post-ERCP rectal indomethacin in eligible patients; selected pancreatic duct stenting

rows.label: Mimics
items: Perforated ulcer: rigid abdomen/free air
Mesenteric ischemia: pain-exam mismatch; MI: ischemic ECG/troponin pattern

table.title: Severity and collections
rows: Transient dysfunction ≤48 hours or local complication

pleural-effusion.name: Pleural effusion
pleural-effusion.scope: Transudate vs exudate (Light criteria), parapneumonic effusion, empyema, malignant effusion
pleural-effusion.core: Fluid in the pleural space causes dyspnea, dullness, and reduced breath sounds; classify by mechanism and identify infection requiring drainage.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Heart failure, cirrhosis, nephrotic syndrome; pneumonia, malignancy, pulmonary embolism, TB
Recent thoracic surgery, pancreatitis, esophageal rupture, autoimmune disease

rows.label: Clues
items: Pleuritic pain, reduced tactile fremitus; large effusion may shift mediastinum away
Fever or persistent sepsis despite antibiotics suggests complicated parapneumonic fluid
Bloody fluid suggests malignancy, embolism, or trauma; milky fluid suggests chyle

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Transudate: altered hydrostatic/oncotic pressure; exudate: increased permeability or impaired lymphatic drainage

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Chest radiograph → **ultrasound-guided thoracentesis** for new unexplained, unilateral, or atypical effusion
Classic bilateral heart-failure effusions → diuresis first; sample if fever, asymmetry, or treatment failure
★ **Exudate if any Light criterion** positive; compare paired pleural and serum measurements
Pleural pH, glucose, cell differential, Gram stain/culture; cytology if cancer suspected
Diuresis can create pseudoexudate; serum–pleural albumin gradient >1.2 g/dL supports transudate

rows.label: Tx
items: Treat systemic cause; therapeutic thoracentesis for significant symptoms; avoid rapid excessive drainage
★ Pus, positive culture, or **pH ≤7.20** → chest tube plus antibiotics
Loculated infected fluid → intrapleural tPA/DNase; persistent sepsis → VATS evaluation
★ Recurrent symptomatic malignancy → **indwelling pleural catheter** or pleurodesis; trapped lung favors catheter

rows.label: Complications
items: Empyema, loculation, trapped lung, respiratory compromise
Thoracentesis → pneumothorax, bleeding, reexpansion pulmonary edema

rows.label: Prevention
items: Heart-failure control, prompt pneumonia treatment; ultrasound guidance reduces procedural injury

rows.label: Mimics
items: Atelectasis: mediastinal shift toward volume loss
Consolidation: increased fremitus, bronchial breath sounds
Pneumothorax: hyperresonance rather than dullness

pleural-effusion.evidence: Not checked online; established pleural disease teaching.

psoriasis.name: Psoriasis
psoriasis.scope: Plaque psoriasis, nail pitting and onycholysis, Auspitz sign, Koebner phenomenon, psoriatic arthritis, topical and systemic therapy
psoriasis.core: Sharply demarcated erythematous plaques with silvery scale, usually on extensor surfaces or scalp; inspect nails and screen for inflammatory arthritis.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Family history, obesity, smoking, alcohol; stress, trauma, streptococcal infection
Lithium, beta blockers, antimalarials; systemic glucocorticoid withdrawal can trigger severe rebound

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Nail pitting, onycholysis**, oil-drop discoloration support diagnosis
Auspitz sign: pinpoint bleeding after scale removal; Koebner phenomenon: lesions at trauma sites
Psoriatic arthritis: morning stiffness, DIP disease, dactylitis, enthesitis, asymmetric or axial involvement
Generalized pustules, erythroderma, fever, hemodynamic disturbance → urgent evaluation

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Immune-mediated TNF/IL-23/Th17 activation → accelerated keratinocyte turnover

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Clinical diagnosis**; biopsy if atypical; assess body surface area and functional impact
KOH scraping if fungal infection possible; inflammatory joint symptoms warrant rheumatology assessment
Before biologics: TB, hepatitis screening; before methotrexate: CBC, liver and renal tests, pregnancy assessment

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Localized plaques → **topical corticosteroid + calcipotriene**; choose potency by site
Face/folds: low-potency steroid briefly or tacrolimus; emollients and scale removal aid penetration
★ Extensive/refractory disease → **narrowband UVB**, methotrexate, or targeted biologic; arthritis requires systemic control
Methotrexate contraindicated in pregnancy and significant liver disease; cyclosporine useful for rapid short-term control
Avoid routine systemic steroids; unstable erythrodermic/pustular disease → hospital support and specialist treatment

rows.label: Complications
items: Joint destruction, depression, cardiometabolic disease; severe skin failure → fluid loss and infection
Systemic immunosuppression → infections; methotrexate → hepatotoxicity, marrow suppression

rows.label: Prevention
items: Smoking cessation, weight management, limit alcohol; screen BP, lipids, diabetes, depression; reduce skin trauma

rows.label: Mimics
items: Tinea corporis: annular advancing edge, positive KOH
Seborrheic dermatitis: greasy scale in sebaceous areas
Atopic dermatitis: flexural eczema with marked pruritus

psoriasis.evidence: Not checked online; established dermatology and psoriatic arthritis teaching.

salicylate-toxicity.name: Salicylate toxicity
salicylate-toxicity.scope: Aspirin overdose, mixed respiratory alkalosis and metabolic acidosis, tinnitus, hyperpyrexia, urinary alkalinization, hemodialysis indications
salicylate-toxicity.core: Aspirin exposure with tinnitus, tachypnea, fever, and a mixed respiratory alkalosis–anion-gap metabolic acidosis; normal pH can conceal severe poisoning.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Intentional overdose; chronic excess aspirin or bismuth subsalicylate, especially with renal impairment
Enteric-coated preparations or bezoars → delayed peak concentrations; older adults vulnerable to chronic toxicity

rows.label: Clues
items: Nausea, vomiting, diaphoresis; confusion, seizures, hypoxemia or hyperpyrexia signal severe toxicity
Children may have predominantly metabolic acidosis; chronic exposure may resemble delirium or sepsis

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Medullary respiratory stimulation + oxidative phosphorylation uncoupling → hyperventilation, organic acids, heat generation
Acidemia increases nonionized salicylate → CNS entry; glucose utilization rises despite normal serum glucose

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Serial salicylate levels**, ABG/VBG, electrolytes/anion gap, glucose, creatinine; check acetaminophen co-ingestion
Repeat concentrations until declining with clinical improvement; one early low level cannot exclude poisoning
★ **Severity overrides the level**; falling serum concentration with worsening acidemia can reflect tissue redistribution

rows.label: Tx
items: Airway assessment, IV fluids, potassium correction; activated charcoal early if airway protected
★ **IV sodium bicarbonate** → serum/urine alkalinization; target urine pH 7.5–8; maintain potassium
★ **Hemodialysis**: altered mentation, oxygen-requiring lung injury, failed alkalinization, or pH ≤7.20
Dialyze if level >100 mg/dL; >90 mg/dL with impaired renal function; chronic toxicity needs lower thresholds
★ Intubation only if essential; **maintain hyperventilation**; neuroglycopenia → dextrose despite normal blood glucose

rows.label: Complications
items: Noncardiogenic pulmonary edema, cerebral edema, renal failure, hypoglycemia, death
Sedation or inadequate ventilation → rapid acidemia and cardiovascular collapse

rows.label: Prevention
items: Avoid aspirin for childhood viral illness; secure medications; reconcile OTC salicylate-containing products
Intentional ingestion → psychiatric assessment and suicide safety planning after medical stabilization

rows.label: Mimics
items: Sepsis: infectious source; may share respiratory alkalosis and lactic acidosis
DKA: marked ketonemia and insulin deficiency; absent salicylate exposure
Toxic alcohols: osmolar gap early; methanol visual injury or ethylene glycol oxalate nephropathy

salicylate-toxicity.evidence: Dialysis thresholds checked 2026-10-30: [EXTRIP salicylate recommendations](https://www.extrip-workgroup.org/salicylates); other management: established toxicology teaching.

shock.name: Shock
shock.scope: Hypovolemic, cardiogenic, distributive (septic, anaphylactic, neurogenic), obstructive, fluid resuscitation, vasopressors
shock.core: Circulatory failure causing tissue hypoperfusion; normal blood pressure does not exclude early shock.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Hemorrhage, GI losses, MI, infection, allergen exposure, spinal injury, thromboembolism
Recent surgery, immunosuppression, indwelling devices increase occult infection risk

rows.label: Clues
items: Tachycardia, altered mentation, oliguria, cool mottled skin; distributive forms may initially feel warm
★ **Anaphylaxis**: rapid airway swelling, wheezing, hypotension; skin findings may be absent
Neurogenic: hypotension with **bradycardia**, warm skin after spinal cord injury

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Oxygen delivery falls below demand → anaerobic metabolism, lactate accumulation
Distributive vasodilation → relative hypovolemia despite normal total body fluid

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Bedside ultrasound**: cardiac function, pericardial fluid, RV dilation, lung sliding, volume assessment
Serial lactate, capillary refill, urine output; CBC, chemistry, ECG, troponin; cultures if infection suspected
Septic shock: vasopressors for MAP ≥65 plus lactate >2 despite volume resuscitation

rows.label: Tx
items: Airway/oxygen, IV access; **balanced crystalloid**, dynamic fluid-response reassessment; restrict with pulmonary congestion
★ Hemorrhage → **control bleeding + balanced blood products**; avoid large crystalloid loads
★ Septic shock → antibiotics within 1 hour, drainage/debridement; crystalloid 30 mL/kg within 3 hours
★ Persistent septic hypotension → **norepinephrine**, MAP ≥65; add vasopressin, then epinephrine; refractory → hydrocortisone

rows.label: Complications
items: AKI, ischemic hepatitis, DIC, ARDS, bowel ischemia, multiorgan failure
Excess fluids → edema; vasopressors → digital/mesenteric ischemia

rows.label: Prevention
items: Early infection treatment, catheter hygiene, VTE prophylaxis, hemorrhage control
After anaphylaxis: trigger avoidance, epinephrine autoinjector, allergy referral

rows.label: Mimics
items: Vasovagal syncope: transient bradycardia, rapid recovery supine
Hypoglycemia: low bedside glucose, improvement with dextrose

table.title: Hemodynamics and cause-directed rescue
rows: Decompress pneumothorax; drain tamponade; reperfuse PE

shoulder-pain.name: Shoulder pain
shoulder-pain.scope: Rotator cuff tendinopathy and tear, impingement, adhesive capsulitis, dislocation, biceps tendinopathy, glenohumeral osteoarthritis
shoulder-pain.core: Active versus passive range of motion, true weakness, trauma history, and pain location distinguish major shoulder disorders.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Overhead work/sports, repetitive lifting, aging; fall or traction → acute structural injury
Diabetes, thyroid disease, prolonged immobilization → capsular fibrosis
Seizure/electrocution → posterior dislocation; anterior instability follows abduction/external rotation injury

rows.label: Clues
items: Lateral upper-arm pain often shoulder origin; radiation below elbow suggests cervical source
Night pain with preserved passive motion suggests cuff disease; weakness persisting after analgesia suggests tear
★ **Fever, hot joint, severe pain with any motion** → urgent septic arthritis evaluation
★ Deformity, absent pulse, deltoid numbness → dislocation with possible neurovascular injury

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Tendon degeneration/tearing impairs dynamic stabilization; capsule contracture restricts joint excursion
Loss of articular cartilage causes mechanically painful glenohumeral degeneration

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Plain radiographs** for trauma, arthritis, deformity; include axillary or scapular-Y view for dislocation
Compare strength, provocative tests, neck examination; document axillary nerve and distal pulses
Ultrasound or MRI for suspected tear, persistent symptoms, or surgical planning; avoid routine immediate MRI

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Most atraumatic disorders → **activity modification, NSAIDs, physical therapy**; maintain motion
Selected painful tendinopathy/capsulitis → corticosteroid injection; avoid repeated injections into tendons
★ Dislocation → **prompt closed reduction**, brief sling, rehabilitation; recheck neurovascular function afterward
Acute traumatic full-thickness tear with functional loss → early orthopedic referral; severe OA → arthroplasty consideration

rows.label: Complications
items: Recurrent instability, axillary nerve injury, greater-tuberosity fracture, persistent weakness
Prolonged sling use → stiffness; chronic massive tear → cuff arthropathy

rows.label: Prevention
items: Rotator cuff/scapular strengthening, ergonomic changes, gradual return to overhead activity
Early supervised motion after injury when safe; avoid unnecessary immobilization

rows.label: Mimics
items: Cervical radiculopathy: dermatomal symptoms, neck-provoked pain
ACS: exertional referred discomfort, diaphoresis, no motion-dependent localization
Pancoast tumor: smoking, hand weakness, Horner syndrome

table.title: Localizing examination
rows: Painful arc; positive Hawkins/Neer; strength preserved
Drop-arm or lag; objective resisted-movement weakness
Both active/passive motion limited, especially external rotation
Flattened deltoid; arm abducted, externally rotated
Anterior groove tenderness; pain with resisted supination

shoulder-pain.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [AAOS rotator cuff guideline 2025](https://www.aaos.org/quality/quality-programs/rotator-cuff/); other examination patterns established teaching.

sickle-cell-disease.name: Sickle cell disease
sickle-cell-disease.scope: Vaso-occlusive pain crisis, acute chest syndrome, splenic sequestration, aplastic crisis, stroke, sickle cell trait, hemoglobin electrophoresis
sickle-cell-disease.core: HbS polymerization causes chronic hemolysis and episodic vascular occlusion; fever, hypoxemia and focal neurologic deficits require urgent escalation.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Autosomal recessive β-globin disease; dehydration, hypoxemia, cold and infection trigger sickling
Functional asplenia increases encapsulated bacterial infection risk from early childhood

rows.label: Clues
items: Baseline anemia, reticulocytosis, jaundice; childhood dactylitis or recurrent severe bone pain
Acute chest syndrome: **new pulmonary infiltrate** plus fever, respiratory symptoms or hypoxemia
Sequestration: sudden splenomegaly, falling hemoglobin, shock; aplasia: **low reticulocyte count**, often parvovirus

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Deoxygenated hemoglobin polymerizes → rigid erythrocytes, endothelial injury, ischemia and shortened RBC survival

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Hemoglobin electrophoresis/HPLC confirms genotype; newborn screen detects disease before symptoms
Crisis → CBC, reticulocytes, bilirubin; fever → blood cultures; respiratory symptoms → chest radiograph
New focal deficit → emergency brain imaging, without delaying transfusion preparation
Distinguish osteomyelitis from infarction using cultures and MRI when focal fever/pain persists

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Pain crisis → rapid **opioid analgesia**, NSAID adjunct, euvolemic hydration; oxygen only for hypoxemia
★ Acute chest → oxygen, **ceftriaxone + azithromycin**, incentive spirometry; transfuse for significant anemia
Severe/progressive acute chest or acute stroke → **urgent exchange transfusion**
Splenic sequestration → cautious simple transfusion; aplastic crisis → supportive transfusion
Fever → prompt parenteral antibiotics; uncomplicated pain crisis alone → no routine transfusion

rows.label: Complications
items: Stroke, avascular necrosis, priapism, pigment gallstones, nephropathy, retinopathy
Repeated transfusions → alloimmunization and iron overload; delayed hyperhemolysis can worsen anemia

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Hydroxyurea** raises HbF, reduces crises; monitor CBC
Penicillin prophylaxis through age 5 in HbSS; pneumococcal, meningococcal, Hib and influenza vaccines
Annual transcranial Doppler ages 2–16 in HbSS/HbSβ0; abnormal → chronic transfusion program

rows.label: Mimics
items: Osteomyelitis: persistent localized pain, fever; Salmonella or S. aureus
Iron deficiency: low ferritin, no hemolytic pattern

tick-borne-diseases.name: Tick-borne diseases
tick-borne-diseases.scope: Lyme disease, Rocky Mountain spotted fever, babesiosis, anaplasmosis, ehrlichiosis, doxycycline therapy
tick-borne-diseases.core: Outdoor exposure followed by multisystem illness: use rash pattern, blood counts, smear and cardiac/neurologic findings to distinguish vector-borne pathogens.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Northeast/upper Midwest Ixodes: Lyme, Babesia, Anaplasma; coinfection possible
Southeast/south-central US: RMSF, ehrlichiosis; absent bite recall cannot exclude
Asplenia, older age, immunosuppression → severe babesiosis

rows.label: Clues
items: Fever, headache, myalgias; hypotension, confusion or organ failure → hospitalize
Persistent fever on doxycycline or disproportionate anemia → consider coinfection

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Rickettsiae infect endothelium; Ehrlichia/Anaplasma infect leukocytes; Babesia infects RBCs
Borrelia spirochetes disseminate to skin, nervous system, heart, joints

rows.label: Dx
items: Early negative Lyme antibodies cannot exclude disease; isolated IgM after 30 days often misleading
★ **CBC, liver tests, creatinine**; anemia → hemolysis labs/smear; quantify babesial parasitemia

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Suspected **RMSF/ehrlichiosis/anaplasmosis → doxycycline immediately**, including children; never await results
Erythema migrans → doxycycline 10 days or amoxicillin 14 days; arthritis → oral treatment 28 days
Lyme high-grade block/PR ≥300 ms → admit, IV ceftriaxone ± pacing; meningitis → doxycycline/ceftriaxone
★ **Babesia: atovaquone + azithromycin**; consider exchange for parasitemia >10%, severe hemolysis or organ failure

rows.label: Complications
items: RMSF: DIC/renal failure; Lyme: facial palsy; Babesia: ARDS, relapse in immunosuppressed patients

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **DEET/picaridin, permethrin clothing, tick checks**, prompt removal with tweezers
High-risk Lyme bite: endemic Ixodes, attached ≥36 hours → single doxycycline dose within 72 hours
No prophylaxis for rickettsial disease; no Lyme testing after asymptomatic bite

rows.label: Mimics
items: Viral syndrome: worsening illness/cytopenias still warrant tick evaluation
TTP: schistocytes rather than intraerythrocytic parasites
Septic arthritis: toxic monoarthritis → aspirate rather than presume Lyme

table.title: Pathogen signatures
rows: Expanding erythema migrans, not necessarily bullseye

tumor-lysis-syndrome.name: Tumor lysis syndrome
tumor-lysis-syndrome.scope: Hyperuricemia, hyperkalemia, hyperphosphatemia, hypocalcemia, acute kidney injury, allopurinol, rasburicase, aggressive hydration
tumor-lysis-syndrome.core: Rapid malignant-cell destruction causes an electrolyte and urate emergency; anticipate risk before cancer treatment and respond immediately to evolving organ dysfunction.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Burkitt/high-grade lymphoma, acute leukemia, bulky chemosensitive tumors, high LDH or leukocyte count
Renal impairment, dehydration, high baseline urate; cytotoxics, steroids, targeted drugs; sometimes spontaneous

rows.label: Clues
items: Nausea, vomiting, weakness, muscle cramps, paresthesias or tetany shortly after treatment
★ **Oliguria, arrhythmia, seizure** signal clinical disease; abnormalities may precede symptoms

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Intracellular potassium/phosphate and nucleic acids released; purine breakdown produces uric acid
Urate and calcium-phosphate precipitation injure kidneys; phosphate binding reduces serum calcium

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Check **K, phosphate, calcium, uric acid, creatinine**, LDH; ECG and continuous telemetry
Laboratory TLS: ≥2 abnormalities within 24 hours, from 3 days pretreatment through 7 days posttreatment
Clinical TLS: laboratory pattern plus AKI, arrhythmia/sudden death, or seizure
High-risk/established disease → repeat electrolytes and renal indices every 4–6 hours; strict intake/output

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **IV isotonic saline**, individualized to cardiac/renal status; avoid potassium/phosphate-containing fluids
★ Dangerous hyperkalemia → **IV calcium for ECG changes**, insulin/dextrose; dialysis for refractory abnormalities
Established hyperuricemia/high-risk TLS → rasburicase; screen **G6PD**, contraindicated if deficient
Phosphate restriction/binders; avoid treating asymptomatic hypocalcemia; symptomatic tetany/seizures → cautious calcium
Urgent dialysis: refractory K/phosphate, acidosis, symptomatic hypocalcemia, fluid overload, or worsening oliguric AKI

rows.label: Complications
items: Acute renal failure, life-threatening ventricular arrhythmia, seizures, sudden death
Rasburicase → hemolysis/methemoglobinemia; allopurinol → hypersensitivity and xanthine crystal burden

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Risk-stratify before treatment; **allopurinol + hydration** for intermediate risk; rasburicase for high risk
Allopurinol prevents new urate formation; does not remove existing uric acid
Avoid urinary alkalinization → calcium-phosphate precipitation; no routine concurrent allopurinol and rasburicase

rows.label: Mimics
items: Rhabdomyolysis: markedly elevated CK and myoglobinuria, muscle injury context
Isolated AKI: electrolyte retention without abrupt tumor-destruction pattern
Sepsis: infection-associated organ dysfunction; can coexist and trigger tumor lysis

vaginitis.name: Vaginitis
vaginitis.scope: Bacterial vaginosis, Trichomoniasis, Vulvovaginal candidiasis, atrophic vaginitis, genitourinary syndrome of menopause
vaginitis.core: Vaginal discharge or irritation requires distinction among dysbiosis, sexually transmitted protozoal infection, yeast overgrowth, and hypoestrogenic mucosal change.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: BV: new partners, douching; trichomoniasis: sexual exposure
Candida: antibiotics, pregnancy, diabetes, immunosuppression; atrophy: menopause or other hypoestrogenic states

rows.label: Clues
items: Pruritus, dysuria, dyspareunia; discharge appearance overlaps, so symptoms alone insufficient
★ **Fever, lower abdominal pain, cervical motion tenderness** → evaluate PID rather than isolated vaginitis
Postmenopausal bleeding needs assessment beyond assuming atrophy

rows.label: Pathophys
items: BV: lactobacilli depleted, anaerobes expand; Candida causes inflammatory overgrowth; Trichomonas is sexually transmitted
Low estrogen thins epithelium and reduces lactobacilli → mucosal fragility and elevated vaginal pH

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Vaginal pH, saline/KOH microscopy**, history and examination; NAAT improves infectious diagnosis
BV: ≥3 Amsel findings—typical discharge, pH elevation, clue cells, positive amine odor
★ Suspected trichomoniasis + negative wet mount → **NAAT**, not reassurance
Recurrent/complicated Candida → culture or PCR for species; asymptomatic colonization alone needs no treatment

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Trichomoniasis → **oral metronidazole 7 days in women**; treat partners, abstain until completed/resolved
BV → oral metronidazole 7 days or vaginal metronidazole/clindamycin; treat symptomatic pregnancy
Candida → topical azole or oral fluconazole; **pregnancy: topical azole 7 days**, avoid oral fluconazole
GSM → moisturizers/lubricants, then low-dose vaginal estrogen for persistent symptoms; assess contraindication context
Recurrent BV: ACOG 2025 considers male-partner metronidazole + topical clindamycin; older boards omit

rows.label: Complications
items: BV/trichomoniasis associated with adverse pregnancy outcomes and increased STI acquisition
Recurrent symptoms → reassess diagnosis, adherence, reinfection, diabetes or resistant/non-albicans yeast

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Trichomoniasis → **retest women at about 3 months**; condoms, partner management
Avoid douching/irritants; no routine partner treatment for uncomplicated Candida

rows.label: Mimics
items: Cervicitis: endocervical mucopus, friability, positive GC/CT NAAT
Contact dermatitis: external irritation after product exposure, no infectious findings

valvular-heart-disease.name: Valvular heart disease
valvular-heart-disease.scope: Aortic stenosis, aortic regurgitation, mitral stenosis, mitral regurgitation, mitral valve prolapse, physical exam, echocardiography, surgical and transcatheter replacement
valvular-heart-disease.core: Murmur timing, location, radiation, and loading maneuvers localize valve disease; symptoms and ventricular response determine intervention.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Aging calcification/bicuspid valve → AS; rheumatic disease → MS
Endocarditis, aortic root dilation/dissection → AR; ischemia, prolapse, chamber dilation → MR

rows.label: Clues
items: Exertional dyspnea, pulmonary edema, reduced exercise tolerance; abrupt deterioration suggests acute regurgitation
★ **Exertional syncope, angina, or HF** with obstruction → severe symptomatic disease
Squatting/handgrip increase regurgitant murmurs; standing/Valsalva makes MVP click earlier

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Stenosis produces upstream pressure overload; regurgitation produces chamber volume overload
Acute regurgitation lacks compensatory dilation, rapidly elevating filling pressures and reducing forward output

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **TTE Doppler** defines anatomy, severity, EF, chamber dimensions, pulmonary pressures
Severe AS: velocity ≥4 m/s, mean gradient ≥40, or valve area ≤1 cm²; discordance requires reassessment
Severe MS: valve area ≤1.5 cm²; TEE for thrombus before balloon intervention or uncertain anatomy
★ Acute murmur with shock → **urgent echocardiography**; TEE if endocarditis/dissection suspected

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Acute severe AR/MR → **urgent surgery**, stabilize with afterload reduction/diuresis if BP permits
Severe primary MR: **EF ≤60% or LVESD ≥40 mm** triggers intervention even without symptoms
Secondary MR → optimize HF treatment first; selected persistent severe cases benefit from transcatheter edge-to-edge repair
Avoid excessive preload reduction in severe AS; symptomatic relief never replaces needed valve intervention

rows.label: Complications
items: Heart failure, pulmonary hypertension, AF, systemic embolism, endocarditis
Mechanical prosthesis: thrombosis/bleeding; bioprosthesis: structural degeneration

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Warfarin for mechanical valves**; no DOAC substitution; rheumatic MS with AF also requires warfarin
Prosthetic valve or prior endocarditis → selected dental prophylaxis; native isolated MVP does not qualify
Periodic echo and symptom review; treat rheumatic fever to prevent recurrent valve injury

rows.label: Mimics
items: HCM: systolic murmur increases with Valsalva/standing
Aortic sclerosis: ejection murmur without significant gradient; flow murmur: normal valve anatomy

table.title: Valve signatures and definitive options
rows: Early diastolic decrescendo; wide pulse pressure
Suitable symptomatic rheumatic valve → balloon commissurotomy

valvular-heart-disease.evidence: Not checked online; established echo thresholds and intervention framework.

venous-thromboembolism.name: Venous thromboembolism
venous-thromboembolism.core: Unilateral swollen leg or sudden unexplained dyspnea with pleuritic pain; pulmonary embolism severity determined by hemodynamics, not clot size.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Immobilization, surgery, malignancy, estrogen, pregnancy/postpartum, previous VTE, inherited thrombophilia

rows.label: Clues
items: DVT: asymmetric calf tenderness, warmth; PE: tachycardia, hypoxemia, hemoptysis, sometimes normal oxygen saturation
Syncope, elevated JVP, cool extremities → impending RV failure; normal chest radiograph does not exclude PE

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Stasis/endothelial injury/hypercoagulability → venous clot; pulmonary obstruction → V/Q mismatch, RV pressure overload

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Wells/pretest probability** first; very low-risk + PERC-negative → no testing
★ Low/intermediate probability → **D-dimer**; negative excludes; positive/high probability → **CT pulmonary angiography**
Age >50: D-dimer threshold age × 10 ng/mL FEU; contrast contraindication → V/Q scan
DVT → compression US; negative proximal scan + persistent suspicion → repeat in 1 week

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Oxygen/support circulation; unstable and unsafe for CT → bedside **echo**; high suspicion/delayed imaging → anticoagulate
★ Most stable VTE → **apixaban/rivaroxaban**; pregnancy → LMWH; severe renal failure → UFH
Lysis contraindicated/fails → catheter thrombectomy/surgical embolectomy; active intracranial bleeding precludes lysis
Acute proximal DVT/PE + absolute anticoagulation contraindication → temporary **IVC filter**, remove when feasible

rows.label: Complications
items: Postthrombotic syndrome; persistent dyspnea → evaluate chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension
Anticoagulation/thrombolysis → bleeding; heparin → HIT

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Major transient trigger → **3 months** anticoagulation; unprovoked/persistent risk → extended course if low bleeding risk
Hospital prophylaxis: LMWH; active bleeding → intermittent pneumatic compression; early mobilization

rows.label: Mimics
items: Cellulitis: predominantly skin erythema, portal of entry
Ruptured Baker cyst: posterior knee symptoms, cyst on US
Pneumonia: focal infiltrate and infectious prodrome

table.title: Treatment branches; 2026 PE guidance uses categories A–E
rows: Stable; low PESI/sPESI; no RV injury
Normotensive + RV dysfunction and/or troponin elevation
Sustained SBP <90 mm Hg or shock

wernicke-korsakoff-syndrome.name: Wernicke-Korsakoff syndrome
wernicke-korsakoff-syndrome.scope: Wernicke encephalopathy (triad of encephalopathy, ataxia, oculomotor dysfunction), Korsakoff psychosis (confabulation, amnesia), thiamine (B1) deficiency, IV thiamine before glucose, mammillary body atrophy
wernicke-korsakoff-syndrome.core: Malnourished adult with confusion, gait ataxia, or ophthalmoplegia/nystagmus; the complete Wernicke triad is often absent.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Alcohol use disorder, hyperemesis gravidarum, bariatric surgery, starvation, inadequate parenteral nutrition
Carbohydrate loading or refeeding increases thiamine demand in depleted patients

rows.label: Clues
items: Hypothermia, hypotension, or coma signal severe deficiency
★ Korsakoff: disproportionate **anterograde amnesia**, retrograde memory loss, confabulation; relatively preserved alertness

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Thiamine deficiency impairs carbohydrate metabolism → ATP failure and selective neuronal injury
Medial thalami, periaqueductal gray, mammillary bodies injured → persistent amnestic syndrome

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Clinical diagnosis**; do not wait for vitamin assays or imaging before treatment
MRI may show symmetric thalamic/periaqueductal lesions; normal MRI does not exclude Wernicke
Chronic disease: mammillary body atrophy; evaluate glucose, electrolytes, magnesium, and competing encephalopathy causes

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Suspected Wernicke → **high-dose IV thiamine**, followed by oral replacement after stabilization
Give thiamine before or with glucose when feasible; never delay emergency dextrose for hypoglycemia
Replete magnesium, fluid/electrolyte deficits; restore nutrition cautiously and treat alcohol withdrawal separately
Ocular findings may improve rapidly; gait/cognition recover more slowly; established amnesia often persists

rows.label: Complications
items: Untreated encephalopathy → death or irreversible Korsakoff syndrome; falls and impaired independent living
Refeeding syndrome → hypophosphatemia, arrhythmias, respiratory weakness

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Routine oral **thiamine supplementation** for persistent malnutrition; nutritional assessment during alcohol treatment
Alcohol cessation support, balanced nutrition; monitor intake after bariatric surgery or prolonged vomiting

rows.label: Mimics
items: Alcohol withdrawal delirium: autonomic hyperactivity, tremor, hallucinations after reduced intake
Hepatic encephalopathy: cirrhosis, asterixis, precipitating bleed or infection
Posterior circulation stroke: abrupt focal deficits; diffusion MRI identifies infarction

wernicke-korsakoff-syndrome.evidence: Not checked online; established thiamine-deficiency teaching.
